He stretched out his hand to repay them, and they defiled his laws.
They were divided by the anger of his face, and it reached their hearts. Their words were softer than oil, but they themselves were like arrows.
Cast your cares on the Lord, and he will feed you; he will never allow the righteous to be shaken.
You, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Let bloodthirsty and deceitful men not live out half their days. But I have trusted in you, Lord.
For the end. For the people who had withdrawn from the sanctuary. When the foreigners seized him in Gath. An inscription. A psalm of David.
Have mercy on me, God, for a man has trampled me; battles have oppressed me all day long.
My enemies have trampled me all day long, and many have fought against me from the heights.
In the daytime I will not be afraid, for I have trusted in the Lord.
Through God I will praise my words. I have trusted in God and will not be afraid. What can a man do to me?
All day long they despised my words; their plans concerning me were for evil.
Let them become wanderers and roam about in secret. They will lie in wait at my heels, just as they lay in wait for my life.
You will cast them away as nothing; in anger you will subdue the peoples, God.
I will recount my life to you; I will place my tears before you, as you promised me.
My enemies will turn back on the day when I call to you. See, I know that you are my God. I will bless God in my words and praise the Lord in my speech.
I have trusted in God and will not be afraid. What can a man do to me?
My vows are binding on me; I will fulfill them to you, God, with praise.
You rescued my life from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling. May I be pleasing before the Lord in the land of the living.
For the end. Do not destroy. An inscription of David. When he had fled and hidden from Saul in the cave.
Have mercy on me, God, have mercy on me, for my soul has trusted in you. In the shelter of your wings I will take refuge until lawlessness passes.
I cried out to God Most High, to God, my benefactor.
He sent from heaven and saved me; he put those who trampled me to shame. God sent his mercy and his truth.
And he rescued my life from among wild beasts, for I lay down troubled. The teeth of the sons of men are weapons and arrows, and their tongues are like a sharp sword.
You are exalted in the heavens, God, and your glory is over all the earth.
They prepared a snare for my feet and bowed my soul down. They dug a pit before me and fell into it themselves.
My heart is ready, God; my heart is ready to praise you and sing psalms to you with my glory.
Awake, my glory! Awake with psalms and praise! And I will awake at dawn.
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, Lord, and sing psalms to you among the nations.
Your mercy has grown great, reaching to heaven, and your faithfulness to the clouds.
You are exalted in heaven, God, and your glory is over all the earth.
For the end. “Do not destroy.” An inscription of David.
Do you truly speak righteousness and judge uprightly, you sons of men?
For even now you practice lawlessness in your hearts; your hands devise injustice on earth.
Sinners were estranged from birth; they went astray from the womb and spoke lies.
Their fury is like a snake’s, like that of a viper and an asp, for it has stopped its ears,
so that it will not hear the voice of a skilled charmer or take a remedy from a wise healer.
May God shatter their teeth in their mouths; break the lions’ fangs, Lord.
Let them become worthless like water that flows away; when he draws his bow, let them grow weak,
like wax that melts, and let them be consumed.
Fire fell, and they did not see the sun. Before he had taken notice of their thorns, he will burn them like buckthorn with the living one’s wrath [?].
The righteous person will rejoice when he sees the repayment, and he will wash his hands in the sinner’s blood.
And a person will say, “Indeed, there is fruit for the righteous, and there is a God who judges them on earth.”
For the end. “Do not destroy.” An inscription of David, at the time when Saul sent men and surrounded his house to kill him.
Deliver me from my enemies, God; save me from those who have risen against me.
Rescue me from those who practice lawlessness; deliver me from bloodthirsty men.
They wanted to hunt down my life, and mighty men came upon me—not because of my sins or transgressions.
Without sin I ran and acted uprightly. Awake to meet me, and see.
You, Lord of hosts, God of Israel, look and visit all the nations. Have no mercy on any who practice lawlessness.
They will return at evening, grow hungry like dogs, and roam around the city.
They will clamor with their mouths, and a sword is on their lips. But now, who has heard this?
For you, Lord, will laugh at them and scorn all the nations.
I will keep my strength for you, for God is my helper.
My God’s mercy will come to meet me, and my God will let me look upon my enemies.
Do not kill them, lest they forget your people. Scatter them by your power and bring them low, for you are my protector, Lord.
For the sins of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be caught in their own arrogance; let them be given over to curses and lies.
Let them be consumed in utter wrath and not be found. Let them know that God rules over Jacob and all the ends of the earth.
They will return at evening, grow hungry like dogs, and go around the city.
They will scatter in search of food, and if they are not satisfied, they will grumble.
I will sing the praises of the Lord; in the morning I will rejoice in your mercy, for you have been my protector.
And a house of refuge on the day of my distress.
My helper, I will sing a psalm to you, God my refuge, the God of my mercy.
For the end, concerning [?] times, for instruction.
When he set fire to Mesopotamia and Assyria of Zobah, and on his return Joab struck twelve thousand in the Valley of Salt. An inscription. A psalm of David.
God, you rejected us and devastated us; you were angry, but you will have compassion on us.
You shook the earth and troubled it. Heal its wounds, for it has been shaken.
You showed your people hardship and gave us wine of folly to drink.
You gave those who fear you a sign, so that they might escape from the bow.
So that your beloved may be delivered, save us with your right hand and hear us.
God spoke from his holiness: I will rejoice; I will be exalted; I will divide Shechem and measure the valleys of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the strength of my head; Judah is my king; Moab is the basin of my hope.
I will direct my steps toward Edom, and foreign peoples have submitted to me.
Who will bring me into the fortified city, or who will lead me as far as Edom?
Is it not you, God, who rejected us and did not go out with our armies, God?
Give us help in distress, for human deliverance is vain.
With God we will act mightily, and he will despise those who afflict us.
For the end, with praises. A psalm of David.
Hear my prayers, O God, and attend to my prayers, O Lord.
From the ends of the earth I cried to you when my heart grew weary. You raised me high upon a rock and guided me.
You have been my hope and a mighty tower for me against the enemy.
I will dwell in your tents forever and take shelter beneath the shade of your wings.
You, O God, heard my prayers; you gave an inheritance to those who fear your name.
You have added days upon days to the king, and to his years the days of generations, down to his own generations.
He stands and remains forever before God. Who will seek mercy and truth from him?
Thus I will sing psalms to you forever and ever, and offer you my prayers day by day.
For the end. Concerning Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
But submit to God alone, my soul, for my salvation comes from him.
He is my God and my savior, my refuge, so that I will not be greatly shaken.
How long will you all rise up against a man to kill him, as against a leaning wall and a collapsing fence?
But they planned only to strip me of my honor, and they rushed on in their thirst. With their mouths they blessed, but in their hearts they cursed.
But be subject to God, my soul, for my endurance comes from him.
He is my God and my savior, my refuge, so that I will not be shaken.
My strength and my glory come from God. God is my help; my hope is in God.
Trust in him, all assemblies of peoples. Pour out your hearts before him, for God is our helper for all time. Pause.
Yet the sons of men are empty; the sons of men are false. They do wrong with their scales, and together they are emptiness.
Do not trust in wrongdoing, and do not desire plunder. If wealth flows in, do not set your hearts on it.
God spoke once, and I heard these two things: strength belongs to God,
and mercy belongs to you, Lord, and you repay each person according to their deeds.
A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judea.
God, my God, I come to you early in the morning. My soul thirsted for you; how much more did my body also, like a barren and waterless land,
where there is no path. So I will appear before you in the sanctuary, to see your strength and your glory.
For your mercy is better for me than my life, and my lips will praise you.
Thus I will bless you throughout my life, and in your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul will be filled as with fat and richness; with joyful lips my mouth will bless you.
For when I remembered you on my bed, I spoke with you early at dawn.
For you have been my helper; in the shelter of your wings I will rejoice.
My soul followed after you, and your right hand upheld me.
But they sought my life in vain; they will enter the depths beneath the earth.
They will be handed over to the sword and become portions for foxes.
The king put his hope in the Lord. All who swear by him will be praised; the mouths of those who spoke injustice will be shut.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Hear my prayers, O God, as I plead with you; rescue my life from fear of the enemy.
Hide me from the gathering of the wicked, from the multitude of those who commit lawlessness.
They sharpened their tongues like swords and drew their bows for bitter deeds,
to shoot in secret at those who are upright in heart. They will shoot at them suddenly and will not be afraid.
They strengthened themselves in evil words; they plotted to hide a snare for me and said, “The Lord does not see this.”
They searched out lawlessness and grew weary in pursuing their search.
A man will approach the depths of his heart, and God will be exalted.
Children’s arrows became their wounds; their own tongues became powerless against them, and all who look upon them will be troubled.
Everyone became afraid, and they recounted the works of God and considered what he had done.
The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him; all who are upright in heart will glory in him.
For the end. A psalm of David. A song of praise of Jeremiah and Ezekiel and of the people when they were about to leave their exile.
Praise befits you, O God, in Zion, and prayers will be offered to you in Jerusalem.
Hear my prayers, for all flesh will come to you.
The words of the lawless have prevailed against us; you will atone for our ungodliness.
Blessed is the one whom you chose and received; he will dwell in your courts. We will be filled with the goodness of your house; your temple is holy.
With wondrous righteousness, hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of those far away at sea.
He establishes the mountains by his power and is clothed with strength.
He stirs up the vast sea and stills the sound of its waves; the nations will be troubled.
The inhabitants of the earth will fear your signs; at the dawning of morning and toward evening they will rejoice.
You looked upon the earth and watered it, and greatly increased its abundance. The river of God became full of water. You prepared its food, for this is how it is prepared.
You watered its furrows and multiplied its crops; when it is sprinkled with dew, its vegetation will flourish.
The crown of the year of your goodness will be blessed; your fields will be filled with richness.
The beautiful places of the wilderness will grow rich; the hills will clothe themselves with joy.
The rams of the flocks will be clothed; the valleys will produce abundant wheat. They will shout and sing praise.
For the end. A psalm of David, concerning the resurrection.
Shout to God, all the earth; sing psalms to his name and give glory to his praise.
Say to God, “How fearsome are your works! Because of your great power, your enemies have lied to you.”
Let all the earth worship you, sing psalms to you, and sing psalms to your name.
Come and see the works of God, how awesome they are in their designs, beyond those of all human beings.
He turned the sea into dry land, and they will cross the rivers on foot. There we will rejoice in him.
He rules by his power forever; his eyes watch the nations. Let those who provoked him not exalt themselves.
Bless our God, you nations; make the sound of his praise heard.
He gave my soul life and did not let my feet stumble.
You tested us, God, and examined us as silver is examined.
You brought us into a trap and laid affliction on our backs.
You made people pass over our heads. We passed through fire and water, and you brought us out to rest.
I will enter your house with sacrifices; I will fulfill my vows to you, which my lips promised you,
which my mouth spoke in affliction.
I will offer you burnt offerings [?], with rams and incense, and I will offer you bulls and goats.
Come, listen to me, all you who fear God, and I will tell you what he has done for my soul.
I cried out to him with my mouth and exalted him with my tongue.
If I saw sins in my heart, may the Lord not hear me.
For this reason God heard me and attended to the sound of my requests.
Blessed is God, who did not reject my prayers or withdraw his mercy from me.
For the end. With praise. A psalm of songs.
God, have mercy on us and bless us; let your face shine upon us and have mercy on us,
so that your ways may be known on earth, your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples give thanks to you, God; let all the peoples give thanks to you.
Let the nations rejoice and be glad, for you judge the peoples uprightly and guide the nations of the earth.
Let the peoples give thanks to you, God; let all the peoples thank you.
The earth yielded its fruit, and God, our God, blessed us.
May our God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Let God arise, and let all his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his presence.
As smoke vanishes, let them vanish; as wax melts before fire, so let sinners perish before God.
Let the righteous rejoice and exult before him, and delight in their joy.
Bless God and sing psalms to his name. Make a way for him who rides through the west; the Lord is his name. Let them rejoice before him and tremble in his presence.
God in his holy dwelling is the father of orphans and the judge of widows.
God settles those who live alone in a home and brings out prisoners by his might, likewise the rebellious who dwell in tombs.
O God, when you went out before your people, when you passed through the wilderness,
the earth shook, and the heavens dripped before God at Sinai, before the God of Israel.
You prepared freely given rain, O God, for your inheritance; although it grew weak, you strengthened it.
Your beasts will dwell in it. In your goodness you made provision for the poor, O God.
The Lord will give the word to those who proclaim good news with great power.
The king of the beloved’s armies has divided the beauty of your house as plunder.
Even if you sleep among the allotted portions, the dove’s wings are covered with silver, and its back is the color of gold.
When the heavenly one gathers the kings upon it, they will become snow-white on Zalmon.
The mountain of God is a fertile mountain, a mountain of many peaks and a fertile mountain.
And what do you think, you proud mountains, of the mountain in which God was pleased to dwell? For the Lord himself will dwell in it forever.
The chariots of God are ten thousandfold, with thousands of drivers, and the Lord is among them at Sinai, from his sanctuary.
He ascended to the heights, took captives, took plunder, distributed gifts, and gave them to the children of men, so that even among unbelievers the Lord God might dwell. Blessed is he.
Blessed is the Lord. Day by day may God our Savior lead us.
Our God is a life-giving God, and deliverance from death comes from the Lord.
But God will crush the heads of his enemies and the hairy scalps of those who walk in their lawlessness.
The Lord said, “I will bring them back from the depths of the abysses, and I will snatch my own out from among the fangs,
so that your foot may be wet with blood, and the tongues of your dogs with the blood of your enemies.”
Your processions were seen, O God—the processions of God, our holy King.
The princes went ahead to raise praise among the musicians and singers.
In the assemblies bless God, and bless the Lord, you who come from the springs of Israel.
There is Benjamin, wonderful in his youth; the princes of Judah, his leaders; the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali.
Command, O God, by your power; strengthen what you have established among us.
From your temple in Jerusalem, kings will bring you offerings.
Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the gatherings of bulls, and the herds of heifers. Let those chosen for silver be rejected. Scatter the nations that desire war.
Let messengers come from Egypt; let the Indians be the first to extend their hands to God.
Kingdoms of the earth, bless God and sing psalms to the Lord.
Prepare a way for him who sits in the heaven of heavens, toward the east. Look, he will raise his voice, his mighty voice.
And give glory to God. His majesty is over Israel, and his power reaches to the clouds of heaven.
God is wonderful among his holy ones. The God of Israel will give his people strength to stand firm. Blessed is God.
For the end. Concerning [?]. A psalm of David.
Save me, God, for the waters have reached my soul. I have sunk into the depths of the abyss, where I have no firm footing.
I have come into the depths of the sea, and the currents have submerged me.
I have grown weary from crying out; my throat has become hoarse. My eyes have grown dim as I wait for the Lord my God.
Those who hate me without cause have become more numerous than the hairs of my head. My enemies, who hate me for no reason, have grown strong against me. I repaid them what I had not stolen.
God, you know my foolishness, and my offenses have not been hidden from you.
Do not let those who wait for you be ashamed because of me, Lord, Lord of hosts. Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, God of Israel.
For your sake I have endured reproach, and shame has covered my face.
I became a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother's sons.
Zeal for your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
I humbled myself with fasting, and this became a cause of reproach for me.
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sat at the gates spoke about me; those who drank wine mocked me.
But I prayed to you, Lord, at an acceptable time. God, in your great mercy, hear me in the faithfulness of your salvation.
Rescue me from the mud so that I do not sink. Let me be saved from those who hate me and from the depths of the great waters.
Do not let the swirling waters swallow me, or the deep abysses submerge me, or the well close its mouth over me.
Hear me, Lord, for your mercy is sweet. Look upon me according to your great compassion.
And do not turn your face away from your servant, for I am in distress. Hear me quickly.
Look upon my soul and redeem me; rescue me because of my enemies.
For you know my reproach, my shame, and my disgrace. All who oppress my soul are before you.
My heart endured reproach and misery. I looked for someone who would grieve with me, but there was no one, and no comforter was found for me.
They gave me gall for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their tables before them become a snare, a retribution, and a stumbling block.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and bend their backs continually.
Pour out your anger upon them, and let the fury of your wrath come upon them.
Let their dwellings become desolate, and let no one live in their homes.
For they persecuted the one you struck, and added to the wounds of my suffering.
Add sins to their sins, so that they may not enter into your righteousness.
Let them be erased from your book of life, and let them not be recorded among your righteous ones.
I am poor and afflicted; let your salvation, O God, receive me.
I will bless the name of my God with blessing and exalt him with praise.
This will please God more than a young calf that has horns and hooves.
Let the poor see and rejoice. Seek God, and your souls will live.
For the Lord has heard the needy and has not despised his prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise him, the sea and everything that moves in them.
God saves Zion, and the cities of Judea will be built. They will build and dwell there and possess it.
The offspring of your servants will be established there, and those who love your name will dwell in it.
For the end. A psalm of David, in remembrance of the Lord's deliverance of him.
God, attend to helping me, and Lord, hurry to assist me.
Let those who sought my life be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who planned evil against me turn back and be ashamed.
Let those who said to me, “Aha, aha!” turn back at once in shame.
Let all who seek you exult and rejoice in you, Lord. Let those who love your salvation say at all times, “God is great!”
I am poor and needy. God, help me. You are my helper and my deliverer; my Lord, do not delay.
For the end. A psalm of David, of the sons of Jonadab and of the first captivity.
In you, Lord, I have put my hope; let me never be ashamed. In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me. Incline your ear to me and save me.
Be my God, my refuge and a strong place to save me, for you are my stronghold and my refuge.
My God, deliver me from the hands of the sinner, from the hands of the lawless and unjust.
You are my endurance, Lord, Lord, my hope from my youth.
I have been sustained by you from the womb. From my mother's womb you have been my refuge, and my help comes from you at all times.
I have become like a spectacle to many, and you are my helper and the one who strengthens me.
Let my mouth be filled with praise, so that I may bless your glory and your majesty all day long.
Do not cast me away, Lord, in my old age; do not abandon me when my strength fails.
My enemies spoke against me, and those who besieged my soul plotted together.
And they said, “God has abandoned him. Let us pursue him and overtake him, for there is no one to rescue him.”
My God, do not keep far from me; O God, attend to helping me.
Let those who spoke evil of me be ashamed and come to an end; let those who sought my harm be clothed in shame and disgrace.
I will hope at all times and add to your praises.
My mouth will recount your righteousness and your praises all day long, for I knew no deceit in learning.
But I will enter into the mighty deeds of the Lord; and, Lord, I remembered your righteousness alone.
My God, you taught me from my youth, and even now I will recount your righteousness.
Even when I am gray-haired and old, my God, do not abandon me, until your arm is proclaimed to every generation that is to come.
Your power and your righteousness reach to the heights. You have done great things, God; who is like you?
Though you showed me much distress and suffering, you comforted me again and brought me up from the deep abysses of the earth.
You increased your might; you turned and comforted me, and once again brought me up from the depths of the earth.
And I will give thanks to you with the preparation of psalms, O true God; I will sing psalms to you with praise, O Holy One of Israel.
My lips will rejoice when I sing psalms to you, and so will my soul, which you redeemed.
My tongue also will speak of your righteousness all day long, when those who planned my harm are put to shame and disgraced.
A Psalm of Solomon.
God, give your judgments to the king and your righteousness to the king’s son, to judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.
Let the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills righteousness.
Let him do justice to the poor among the people, save the children of the needy, and humble the arrogant.
Let him stand and remain as long as the sun, and before the moon, from generation to generation.
Let him descend like rain upon a fleece, like dew that moistens the earth.
In his days let righteousness arise, and abundant peace, until the moon comes to an end.
Let him rule from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.
Let the Indians fall down before him first, and let his enemies eat dust.
Let the kings of Tarshish and the islands offer him gifts; let the kings of Arabia and Sheba bring him gifts.
Let all the kings of the earth bow down to him, and let all nations serve him.
For he rescued the poor from the powerful—the poor and the needy who have no helper.
He will have pity on the poor and the needy, and he will save the lives of the needy.
He will rescue their lives from wicked usury; his name is precious in their sight.
He will live, and gold from Arabia will be given to him. They will pray to him at all times and bless him continually.
There will be stability throughout the earth, and on the mountaintops his fruit will rise higher than Lebanon. They will flourish in the city of the Lord like the grass of the earth.
May the Lord’s name be blessed forever, for his name exists before the sun. In him all the nations of the earth will be blessed, and all peoples will call him blessed.
Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
And blessed is the holy name of his glory forever. May the whole earth be filled with his glory. So be it, so be it.
A Psalm of Asaph.
How good God is to Israel and to those who are upright in heart!
But as for me, my feet had almost slipped, and my steps had nearly stumbled.
I envied the lawless when I saw the peace of sinners.
For there was no escape from their death; their torments are enduring.
They do not share in human toil, nor will they be tormented like other people.
Therefore pride seized them; they clothed themselves in their impiety and injustice.
Their injustices will come forth as though from fat, for they followed the thoughts of their own hearts.
They plotted and spoke wickedly of wrongdoing; they made their plans from on high.
They set their mouths against heaven, and their tongues ranged over the earth.
For this reason my people will return here, and my days will be found full and complete among them.
They said, “How does God know? Is there really knowledge with the Most High?”
Look, they are sinners, yet they prosper; they remain and possess the greatness of the world.
I said, “Then it was in vain that I made my heart righteous and washed my hands in innocence.”
And I was tormented continually, and my rebukes came every morning.
Although I said, “I will recount it this way,” behold, I had also pledged myself to the generation of your children.
I considered it, but even this is a struggle for me,
until I enter the sanctuary of God and consider their end.
Yet because of their deceit you will banish them, and you will overthrow them in their arrogance.
How suddenly they became desolate! They were destroyed, dwindled away, and perished because of their lawlessness.
They became like dreams of those who wake up. Lord, in your city you will dishonor their images.
For a fire flared up in my heart, and my kidneys were altered.
I was despised and did not understand; I was considered an animal before you.
Yet I am with you at all times; you took hold of my right hand.
You guided me with your counsel and received me with glory.
What do I have at all in heaven? And what else should I seek from you on earth?
My heart and my flesh failed; God is the God of my heart and my portion forever.
Look, those who have distanced themselves from you will perish; you will destroy all who rebelled against you.
It is good for me to draw near to God and to place my hope in the Lord, to recount all your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion.
Wisdom of Asaph. Why, God, have you rejected us completely? Why has your wrath blazed against the flock of your pasture?
Remember your people, whom you acquired from the beginning. You redeemed the portion of your inheritance, this Mount Zion where you dwelt.
Raise your hand against their pride completely, against all the wrong the enemy has done in your sanctuary.
Those who hate you boasted in the midst of your festival; they set up their own signs as signs.
And they themselves did not know the way out above.
As in a forest, they cut down its doors with axes all together; with axes and hammers they demolished it.
They burned your sanctuary with fire; they desecrated the dwelling of your name on the ground.
Their people said together in their hearts, “Come, let us silence all the festivals of God throughout the land.”
We saw no signs at all, and there is no longer a prophet, and no one will know us at all.
How long, God, will the enemy taunt you and the adversary provoke your holy name?
Why do you turn away your hand and your right hand completely from within your bosom?
God is our king from before the ages, you who brought about salvation in the midst of the earth.
You established the sea by your power; you crushed the heads of dragons upon the waters.
You shattered the heads of the dragon and gave it as food to the armies of the Indians.
You made springs and streams gush forth; you dried up mighty rivers.
The day is yours, and the night is yours; you established the light and the sun.
And you established all the boundaries of the earth; you created spring and summer.
Remember this: the enemy reviled the Lord, and a foolish people provoked your holy name.
Do not hand over to wild beasts the soul that acknowledges you, and do not forget the souls of your needy people forever.
Look upon your covenant, for the houses of the bewildered on earth are filled with lawlessness.
Do not let the needy turn back in shame; rather, let the poor and needy bless your holy name.
Arise, O God, and plead your cause. Remember the insults that come from the fool all day long.
Do not forget the voice of your servants; let the arrogance of those who hate you rise continually.
For the end. “Do not destroy.” A psalm of praise by Asaph.
We will give thanks to you, O God; we will give thanks and call upon your name. I will recount all your wonders.
When I take the appointed time, I will judge uprightly.
The earth and all its inhabitants wasted away; I established its pillars.
I said to the lawless, “Do not act lawlessly,” and to sinners, “Do not raise your horns.”
Do not lift your horns on high, and do not speak unjustly against God.
For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the wilderness of the mountains,
but God is the judge: he humbles one and raises another.
A cup is in the Lord’s hand, filled with unmixed wine poured into it, and he poured from this one into that one. Yet its dregs will not be drained, and all the sinners of the earth will drink it.
I will rejoice forever; I will sing psalms to the God of Jacob.
You will crush all the horns of sinners, and the horn of the righteous will be raised high.
For the end, with praises. A psalm of Asaph; a song concerning the Assyrians.
God is known in Judea, and his name is great in Israel.
Peace was his place, and his dwelling was in Zion.
There the Lord shattered the power of bows, weapons, the sword, and battle.
You shine wonderfully from the everlasting mountains.
Let all who are senseless at heart be troubled. They slept their sleep, and none of the men found anything in the strength of their hands.
At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, even those mounted on horses fell asleep.
You are fearsome, and who can stand before you?
When you appeared from heaven, your wrath became manifest; the earth feared and trembled.
When God arose for judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.
The thoughts of men will acknowledge you, and what is hidden will praise you with wisdom.
Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord our God. All you who are around him, bring offerings to the Awesome One.
He takes away the spirits of rulers; he is more awesome than all the kings of the earth.
For the end. Concerning Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.
With my voice I cried to the Lord; with my voice I cried to God, and he looked toward me.
On the day of my distress I sought God, with my hands raised before him at night, and I was not disappointed. My soul refused to be comforted.
I remembered God and rejoiced; I pondered, and my spirit grew faint within me. Pause.
My eyes reached the night watches; I was troubled and could not speak.
I considered the former days and remembered the years of old.
At night I spoke with my heart; I pondered, and my spirit was distressed within me.
Will the Lord reject me forever, and never again be pleased with me?
Or will he completely withhold his mercy from me? Or has he brought his word to an end, from generation to generation?
Or will my God forget to show compassion ever again? Or will he withhold his compassion in his anger? Pause.
I said, “Now I have begun; this is the renewal of the right hand of the Most High.”
I remembered the works of the Lord; I remembered his wonders from the beginning.
I pondered all your works and reflected on what your hands have made.
O God, your ways are holy. What god is great like our God?
You are God, who works wonders; you have shown your power to your people.
With your arm you redeemed your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Pause.
The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and were afraid, and the depths were troubled at the sound of the mighty waters.
The clouds gave voice, for your arrows also fly.
At the sound of your thunder in the wheel, your lightning appeared to the world; the earth was shaken and trembled.
Your ways are in the sea, and your paths in the mighty waters, and your footprints are no longer visible.
You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
An instruction of Asaph.
Listen, you peoples, to my law; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in a parable and speak parables from the beginning.
As we have heard and known these things, and our fathers have told us,
we have hidden nothing from their children, telling the next generation the praises of the Lord, his power, and the wonders he has done.
He established his testimony in Jacob and laid down a law for Israel, commanding our fathers to make these things known to their children,
So that the children born in another generation may know, and may rise and tell these things to their own children.
so that they might place their hope in God and not forget the works of God, but earnestly seek his commandments,
and not be like their fathers, an evil and rebellious generation, a generation that did not set its heart right and did not keep its spirit steadfast toward God.
The sons of Ephraim, drawing their bows fully and powerfully, turned their quivers back on the day of battle.
They did not remain faithful to the Lord’s covenant and were unwilling to walk according to his ordinances.
They forgot his kindnesses and the wonders he had shown them.
He performed his wonders before their fathers in the land of Egypt and in the plain of Tanis.
He split the sea and brought them through it, and made the waters stand as though in wineskins.
He led them with a cloud by day and with the light of fire throughout the night.
He split the rock in the wilderness and gave them water to drink as though from a great deep.
He brought water out of the rock and made the waters flow like rivers.
Yet they continued to sin and further provoked the Most High in the waterless land.
They tested God in their hearts by asking for food for themselves.
They grumbled against God and said, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
For he struck the rock, and waters flowed and streams rushed from it. But can he also give us bread, or prepare a table for his people?”
Therefore the Lord heard this and delayed; fire blazed in Jacob, and wrath rose against Israel.
For they did not believe in God and did not trust in his salvation.
He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of heaven.
He rained manna upon them for food and gave them the bread of heaven.
People ate the bread of angels, and he sent food down upon them in abundance.
He brought forth the south wind and brought the north wind by his power.
He rained meat upon them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.
He cast them into the midst of their camp and around their tents.
They ate and were fully satisfied, and he gave them what they desired.
They lacked nothing they desired. While the food was still in their mouths,
wrath from God rose against them. He killed many of them and destroyed the very best of Israel.
Despite all this, they sinned still more and did not believe in his wonders.
Their days dwindled away in futility, and their years quickly passed.
When he killed them, they sought him; they turned back and sought God early in the morning.
They remembered that God was their helper, that God Most High was their deliverer.
They loved him with their mouths, but lied to him with their tongues.
Their hearts were not upright toward him, and they were not faithful to his covenant.
But he himself was compassionate: he forgave their sins and did not destroy them. He repeatedly turned away his anger and did not stir up all his wrath.
He remembered that they were flesh, a breath that goes out and does not return.
How often they embittered him in the wilderness and angered the Most High in the waterless land!
They turned back and tested God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his hand on the day when he delivered them from the hands of their oppressors,
how he performed his signs and wonders in the land of the Egyptians and in the plain of Tanis.
He turned their rivers and their rains into blood, so that they could not drink.
He sent dogflies among them, and they devoured them; he ruined them with frogs.
He gave their fruit to blight and their crops to locusts.
He struck their vineyards with hail and their fig trees with frost.
He delivered their livestock over to hail and judged their possessions with fire.
He sent upon them the fury of his anger—wrath, anger, and distress. He sent torments upon them through an evil angel.
He directed the fury of his anger against them. He did not spare their lives from death, and he delivered their livestock over to death.
He struck all the firstborn of the Egyptians, the firstfruits of all their toil, in the dwellings of Ham. Pause.
He drove his people forth like sheep and led them out like a flock into the wilderness.
He guided them with hope, and they were not afraid; the sea covered their enemies.
He brought them to his holy mountain, to the mountain that his right hand had acquired.
He drove out the nations before them, allotted them a share in his inheritance, and settled the people of Israel in their dwellings.
They tested and embittered God Most High and did not keep his testimony.
They turned back and went astray like their fathers; they turned back and became like a crooked bow.
Again they angered him with their altars and provoked him to jealousy with their carved images.
God heard and despised them, and utterly rejected Israel.
He cast away the tabernacle at Shiloh, the tabernacle he had set among human beings.
He delivered their strength into captivity and their beauty into the hands of their enemies.
He gave his people over to the sword and disregarded his inheritance.
Fire devoured their young men, and no one mourned for their virgins.
Their priests fell by the sword, and there was no one to mourn their widows.
The Lord awoke as though from sleep, like a mighty man shaking off wine.
He struck his enemies back and made them an everlasting disgrace.
He rejected Joseph’s tabernacle and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
But he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his sanctuary like a unicorn; he established it on the earth forever.
He chose David his servant and took him from the flocks of sheep.
From following the ewes that had given birth, he took him to shepherd Jacob his servant and Israel his inheritance.
He shepherded them with the wisdom of his heart and led them with the innocence of his hands.
A psalm of Asaph.
God, the nations have entered your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple and made Jerusalem like the huts of those who guard fruit.
They gave the corpses of your servants as carrion to the birds of heaven, and the bodies of your holy ones to the beasts of the earth.
They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
We have become a disgrace to our neighbors, an object of laughter, mockery, and jest to those around us.
How long, Lord? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy blaze like fire?
Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you, on the kings who have not called on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place.
Do not remember our former sins. Let your mercy come quickly to us, Lord, for we have become very poor.
Help us, God our Savior, for the glory of your name. Lord, save us and forgive our sins for your name’s sake.
Never let them say among the nations, “Where is their God?” Instead, let vengeance for the blood of your servants that was shed be made known among the nations before our eyes.
Let the groaning of the prisoners come before you; according to the greatness of your arm, preserve the children of those who were slain.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their laps for the insults with which they insulted you, Lord.
We, your people and the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever; from generation to generation we will proclaim your praises.
For the end. Concerning those who rave. A testimony of Asaph. A psalm concerning the Ethiopians.
You who shepherd Israel, look upon us, you who lead Joseph like a flock. You who sit upon the cherubim, reveal yourself.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your strength and come to save us.
God of hosts, restore us; show your face to us, and we will be saved.
Lord God of hosts, how long will you be angry at the prayers of your servants?
You fed us bread of tears and gave us tears to drink by measure.
You made us a reproach to our neighbors, the butt of our enemies’ jokes.
God of hosts, restore us; show your face to us, and we will be saved.
You transplanted a vine from Egypt; you drove out the nations and planted them.
And you guided it, established its roots, and it filled the land.
Its shade covered the mountains, and its branches covered the cedars of God.
It stretched its vine to the sea, and its shoots reach to the River.
Why did you tear down its fence, so that those passing along the road pluck its fruit?
A boar from the forest ravaged it, and a wild beast grazed on it.
God of hosts, turn back; look down from heaven and see; visit this vineyard.
And care for what your right hand planted, and for the son of man whom you strengthened for yourself.
Burned with fire and laid waste; at your rebuke they will perish.
Let your hand be upon the man at your right hand, upon the son of man whom you strengthened for yourself.
We will no longer turn away from you. You will give us life, and we will call upon your name.
Lord God of hosts, restore us; show your face to us, and we will be saved.
For the end. Concerning the winepresses. A psalm of Asaph, for the fifth day of the week.
Rejoice in God, who is our helper; shout to the God of Jacob.
Take up a psalm and offer praise; sing a psalm to him with a sweet voice.
Blow the trumpet at the beginning of the months, on the marked day of our yearly festivals.
This is a command for Israel and an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
The testimony for Joseph, which he laid upon him when he came out of the land of the Egyptians: he heard a language that he did not know.
I freed his shoulders from burdens, and his hands from serving with [?] and a shovel.
In distress you called to me, and I rescued you. I heard you from the hidden place of the storm, and I tested you at the waters of Contention.
Listen, my people, and I will testify to you; Israel, if only you would listen to me!
You must no longer have temporary gods, and you must not worship a foreign god.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians. Open your mouth, and I will fill it.
My people did not listen to my voice, and Israel paid no attention to me.
I abandoned them to follow the desires of their hearts, for they went according to their own wishes.
For if my people had listened to me, or Israel had walked in my ways,
I would have brought his enemies low as though they were nothing, and laid my hand upon his oppressors.
The enemies of the Lord lied to him, and their time will last forever.
He fed them with the finest wheat; he satisfied them with honey from the rock.
A psalm of Asaph.
God stood in the assembly of the gods, and in their midst he judged them.
How long will you judge unjustly and show favoritism to sinners?
Give justice to the orphan and the widow; uphold the rights of the destitute and the lowly.
Save the poor and the destitute; rescue them from the hands of the sinner.
They did not understand or take it to heart. They walked in darkness, and all the foundations of the earth were shaken.
I said, “You are gods, or all of you are sons of the Most High.”
Yet look, you will die like human beings, and fall like one of the rulers.
Arise, God, and judge the earth, for you will inherit all the nations.
A psalm of praise by Asaph.
God, who is like you? Do not be silent, and do not remain still, God.
For look, your enemies have raised an outcry, and those who hate you have lifted their heads.
They devised cunning plans against your people; they plotted against your holy ones.
And they said, “Come, let us wipe them out from among the nations, so that the name of Israel will no longer be remembered.”
They plotted together with one accord, and made a covenant against you:
The camps of the Edomites and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, and the Philistines, together with all the inhabitants of Tyre.
Assyria too had joined them; all these were a support to the sons of Lot.
Do to them as you did to Midian, to Sisera, and to Jabin in the ravines of Kishon.
They perished at the springs of Dor and became like dung on the ground.
Make their rulers like Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah, and Zalmunna, and all their rulers likewise.
They said, “Let us take possession of God's sanctuary for ourselves.”
My God, make them like a wheel, like a reed before the wind.
As fire burns the forest, as a flame scorches the mountains,
so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your anger.
Fill their faces with dishonor, and they will seek your name, Lord.
Let them be ashamed and troubled forever and ever, and let them perish in disgrace.
Let them know that your name is Lord and that you alone are exalted over all the earth.
For the end. Concerning the winepresses. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
How lovely are your dwellings, Lord of hosts!
My soul longs and yearns for your courts; my heart and my flesh will rejoice in the living God.
For the sparrow has found a home for itself, and the turtledove a nest where it may lay its young—your altar, Lord of hosts, my King and my God.
Blessed are all who dwell in the house of the Lord; they will praise you forever and ever.
Blessed is the man whose help comes from you; he has set his mind on going up.
From the valley of sorrow, in the place where he made his vow, the lawgiver will give blessings.
He will go from strength to strength, and God will appear in Zion.
Lord God of hosts, hear my prayers; listen, God of Jacob.
You are acceptable to us; look, God, and look upon the face of your anointed.
For one day in your courts is better for me than thousands. I chose to be among the refuse in the house of God rather than dwell in the homes of sinners.
The Lord our God loves mercy and truth. The Lord will give grace and glory; he will not withhold his mercy from those who walk blamelessly.
Lord God of hosts, blessed is the man who trusts in you.
For the end. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
You looked with favor, Lord, on your land and brought back the captives of Jacob.
You forgave the wrongdoing of your people; you covered all their sins.
You stilled all your indignation and turned away from your fierce anger.
Turn to us, God our Savior, and turn your indignation away from us.
Do not be angry with us forever, Lord, and do not prolong your anger from generation to generation.
God, you will give us life again, and your people will rejoice in you.
Show us your mercy, Lord, and give us your salvation.
I will hear what the Lord our God says. He will speak peace to his people, to his holy ones, and to those who have turned to him with their hearts.
Indeed, his salvation is near those who fear him, so that his glory may dwell in our land.
Mercy and truth will meet; righteousness and peace will kiss.
Truth sprang up from the earth, and righteousness appeared from heaven.
The Lord will give what is good, and our land will yield its fruit.
Righteousness will go before him, and he will set his footsteps on the path.
A prayer of David.
Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me, for I am poor and needy.
Preserve my life, for I am holy. Save your servant, my God, who has put his hope in you.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I cried out to you all day long.
Make your servant's soul glad, for to you, Lord, I lifted up my soul.
For you, Lord, are kind and upright, abundant in mercy toward all who call on you.
Give ear, Lord, to my prayers, and attend to the voice of my pleas.
On the day of my distress I called to you, and you heard me.
There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, and there are no works like yours.
All the nations you made will come and bow down before you, and they will glorify your name forever.
You are great, Lord, and you do wonders; you alone are God.
Guide me in your way, and I will walk in your truth, and my heart will rejoice in fearing your name.
I will give thanks to you, Lord my God, with my whole heart; I will glorify your name forever.
Your mercy toward me was great; you rescued my soul from the depths of the underworld.
God, the lawless rose up against me, and an assembly of powerful men sought my life, and they did not keep you, God, before them.
But you, Lord my God, are compassionate and merciful, patient, abundant in mercy, and faithful.
Look upon me and have mercy on me. Give strength to your servant; save the son of your maidservant.
Show me a sign of your goodness, so that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because you, Lord, have helped and comforted me.
For the sons of Korah. A psalm of praise.
Its foundations are on his holy mountain. The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
The glorified one spoke about you—behold, O city of God.
I remembered Rahab and Babylon, who know me. Behold, the Philistines, Tyre, and the peoples of India: these were born there.
Zion is called Mother, and a man was born in her; the Most High himself laid her foundations.
The Lord will tell, in the records of the people, of these rulers who were born there.
So that all whose dwelling comes from you may rejoice in you.
For the end, concerning Mahalath. Instruction, because Heman the Ezrahite gave an answer.
Lord, God of my salvation, I cried out by day and stood before you at night.
Let my prayers come before you, Lord; incline your ear to my pleas.
For my soul is filled with suffering, and my life has drawn near to the underworld.
I was counted among those who go down into the pit; I became like a man without a helper.
Free among the dead, like those struck down who sleep in the grave, whom you no longer remember, and who have been cast away from your hand.
You placed me in the deepest pit, in darkness and in the shadows of death.
Your wrath settled upon me; you brought all your surges upon me.
You put my acquaintances far from me, and they made me an object of their scorn. I was handed over and could not get out.
My eyes grew weak from poverty. I cried to the Lord every day and lifted my hands to you.
Will you work your wonders for the dead? Or will physicians raise them up, and will they praise you?
Will anyone ever tell of your mercy in the grave, or of your faithfulness in destruction?
Will your wonders be known in darkness, or your righteousness in a forgotten land?
But I cried to you, Lord; in the morning my prayers will reach you.
Why, Lord, do you reject my soul or turn your face away from me?
I have been poor and burdened with toil from my youth. From a height I was brought low and was stunned.
Your anger settled upon me; your terrors threw me into turmoil.
They surrounded me like water all day long; together they besieged me.
You put my friends and acquaintances far from me because of my misery.
Wisdom of Heman the Ezrahite.
I will praise your mercies forever, Lord; with my mouth I will proclaim your faithfulness from generation to generation.
You said, “The world will be built through mercy; your faithfulness will be established in the heavens.”
I made a covenant with my chosen ones; I swore to David my servant:
“I will establish your descendants forever and build your throne from generation to generation.”
The heavens will acknowledge your wonders, Lord, and your faithfulness in the assemblies of the holy ones.
Who in the clouds is equal to you? Or who among the sons of God is like the Lord?
God is glorified in the council of his holy ones, great and fearsome to those who surround him.
Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are mighty, Lord, and your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule the might of the sea, and you calm the turmoil of its waves.
You bring down the proud like wounded men; with the strength of your arm you scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours; you established the world and all that fills it.
You made the north and the south; Tabor and Hermon will rejoice in your name.
Yours is the arm, and yours is the strength; may your right hand grow strong, and may your hand be lifted high.
Your throne is established in righteousness and justice; mercy and faithfulness will go before your face.
Blessed are the people who know your praises, Lord; they will walk in the light of your face.
And they will rejoice in your name all day long, and through your righteousness they will be exalted.
You are the glory of our strength, and by your favor our horn will be raised high.
Help comes from the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, our king.
Then you spoke in a vision to your sons and said, “I will place help upon the mighty one, and I will exalt the one chosen from my people.”
I found David my servant; with my holy oil I anointed him.
My hand will uphold him, and my arm will strengthen him.
Let no enemy gain an advantage over him, and let no son of lawlessness afflict him.
I will strike down his enemies before him, and I will deliver those who hate him into defeat.
My truth and my mercy are with him, and in my name his horn will be raised high.
I will set his hand over the sea and his right hand over the rivers.
He will call to me, “You are my Father, God, the helper of my salvation.”
I will make him my firstborn, higher than all the kings of the earth.
I will keep my mercy for him forever, and my covenant with him will remain faithful.
I will establish his offspring forever and ever, and his throne like the days of heaven.
If his sons abandon my law and are unwilling to walk according to my judgments,
if they despise my statutes and do not keep my commandments,
I will strike their lawlessness with a rod and their wrongdoing with punishments.
But I will not withhold my mercy from them or betray my truth.
I will not dishonor my covenant, nor will I disregard anything that comes from my lips.
Once I swore by my holiness that I would not lie to David.
His offspring will endure forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me,
like the moon, for it is established forever, a faithful witness in heaven.
But now you have rejected and dishonored your anointed one and struck him down.
You have turned your covenant away from your servant; you have defiled his holiness on the earth.
You have torn down all his walls and made his strongholds tremble.
Those passing along the road have plundered him; he has become a reproach to his neighbors.
You have raised high the right hand of his oppressors and made all his enemies rejoice.
You have withdrawn help from his sword and have not supported him in battle.
You have dishonored his holiness and cast his throne down to the ground.
You have shortened the days of his lifetime and poured shame over him.
How long will you turn your face away—forever? Will your anger blaze like fire?
Now remember and see what my rest is. Did you create all the children of humankind in vain?
Who is the person who will live and not see death, or rescue his own soul from the power of the underworld?
Where are your former mercies, Lord, which you swore to David in your truth?
Remember the insults against your servants, which I have borne in my bosom from many nations.
Your enemies hurled these insults, Lord; they mocked the exchange of your anointed one.
Blessed be the Lord God forever and ever. So be it, so be it.
A prayer of Moses, the man of God.
Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation.
Before the mountains were established, and before you created the earth and the whole world, from eternity to eternity, you are.
And do not turn humanity toward suffering. You said, “Return to me, children of humanity.”
A thousand years in the Lord’s eyes are like yesterday, which has passed, like a watch in the night.
And their years will be held in contempt; in the morning they will spring up like grass.
In the morning they will flourish and blossom like grass; in the evening they will wither, dry up, and fall.
We have wasted away because of your anger, and we have been troubled by your wrath.
You have set our sins before you, and our lives in the light of your face.
All our days have dwindled, and we have been troubled by your anger. The span of our years is unceasing, like a spider.
And the number of the days of our years is seventy years, or, if more, eighty years. Whatever exceeds that is pain and groaning. Gentleness came upon us, and we were disciplined.
But now, who can know the power of your anger, or reckon your wrath according to the fear of you?
Thus show me your right hand, and show your wisdom to those who are humble in heart.
Return, Lord! How long? Comfort your servants.
We were filled with your mercy in the morning; we rejoiced and were glad all the days of our lives.
We were glad in return for the days when you humbled us and the years in which we saw suffering.
Look, Lord, upon your servants and upon the works of your hands, and guide their children.
May the light of the Lord God be upon us. Set the works of our hands right for us, Lord; prosper the works of our hands for us.
A song of praise by David.
Whoever dwells in the help of the Most High will rest in heaven under the shelter of God.
He will say to the Lord, “You are my protector, my refuge, my God, and I trust in him.”
He will rescue me from the hunter’s snare and from troubling words.
He will take you between his shoulders; you will trust in the shelter of his wings. His truth will surround you like armor.
You will not fear the terror of the night or the arrow that flies by day.
From the thing that moves in darkness, from the demon’s stumbling block at midday.
Thousands will fall at your side and tens of thousands at your right hand, but nothing will come near you.
You will only look with your eyes and see the punishment of sinners.
For you, Lord, are my hope; you have made the Most High your refuge.
No evils will reach you, and no afflictions will come near your dwelling.
He has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will carry you in their arms, so that you never strike your foot against a stone.
You will walk upon asps and basilisks; you will trample the lion and the dragon underfoot.
Because he has put his hope in me, I will rescue him; I will shelter him, because he has known my name.
He will call to me, and I will hear him. I will be with him in distress; I will rescue him and glorify him.
I will satisfy him with a long life and show him my salvation.
A psalm of praise for the Sabbath day.
It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing psalms to your name, Most High,
to proclaim your mercy in the morning and your faithfulness at night,
to praise you with a ten-stringed psaltery and with the sound of praise.
You have made me glad, Lord, through your creation, and I will rejoice in the works of your hands.
How great are your works, Lord, and how very deep are your thoughts!
A senseless man does not know this, and a fool does not understand it.
When sinners sprout like grass, when those who commit lawlessness flourish, they will be destroyed forever and ever.
But you are exalted forever, Lord. For behold, your enemies, Lord—for behold, your enemies will perish.
All who commit lawlessness will be scattered.
My horn will be raised high like that of a unicorn, and my old age will be in rich oil.
My eye has looked upon my enemies; my ear will hear of those who have risen against me in wickedness.
The righteous will flourish like palm trees; they will grow abundantly like the cedars of Lebanon.
They will be planted in the house of the Lord and will flourish in the courts of our God.
Even in old age they will be abundant; they will be lush and tender with richness.
To proclaim that the Lord our God is upright, and there is no injustice in him.
On the first day of the week, when the earth was established. A blessing of praise by David.
The Lord reigns; he has clothed himself in majesty. The Lord has clothed himself in strength and girded himself with it.
He established the world so that it would not be shaken. Your throne has been established from the beginning; you are forever.
The rivers have risen, Lord; the rivers have raised their voices. The rivers will rise in their courses.
At the sound of many waters, the surges of the sea became wondrous. You are wondrous, Lord, on high.
We have firmly believed your testimonies. Holiness befits your house, Lord, for many days.
A psalm of David for Wednesday.
God of vengeance, Lord, God of vengeance, you have revealed yourself.
Rise up, you who judge the earth; repay the proud what they deserve.
How long will sinners, Lord, how long will sinners boast?
They will speak out and utter injustice; all who practice lawlessness will speak.
They have brought your people low, Lord, and tormented your inheritance.
They have killed the widow and the stranger; they have slaughtered the orphans.
And they said, “The Lord does not see this, and the God of Jacob takes no notice.”
Understand, you senseless ones among the people! You fools, how long will you fail to understand?
Does he who planted the ear not hear? Or does he who formed the eye not see?
Does he who disciplines the nations not rebuke—he who teaches people knowledge?
The Lord knows people's thoughts, that they are empty.
Blessed is the person whom you discipline, Lord, and whom you teach from your law.
You ease his days of trouble until a pit is dug for the sinner.
The Lord does not reject his people, and he does not disregard his inheritance.
Until justice returns to righteousness, all who are upright in heart will embrace it.
Who will rise with me against the wicked? Or who will stand beside me against those who practice lawlessness?
If the Lord had not helped me, my soul would soon have dwelt in the underworld.
When I said, “Look, my feet have slipped,” your mercy, Lord, helped me.
Amid the many sorrows of my heart, your comfort gladdened my soul.
Can a throne of lawlessness be allied with you, one that causes hardship contrary to your command?
They hunted the life of the righteous and condemned innocent blood.
The Lord became my refuge, and God the helper in whom I hope.
The Lord will repay them according to their lawlessness, and according to their wickedness the Lord our God will destroy them.
A hymn of praise. Of David.
Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us cry out to God our Savior.
Let us come before him with thanksgiving; let us cry out to him with psalms.
The Lord is a great God, a great King over all the earth.
In his hands are all the expanses of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
The sea is his, and he made it; his hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us bow down to him, fall down, and weep before the Lord our Maker.
He himself is the Lord our God; we are the people of his hand and the flock of his pasture.
Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as at the embittering, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me, put me to the proof, and saw my works.
For forty years I contended with that generation and said, “They always go astray in their hearts, and they have not known my ways.”
So I swore in my anger, “They shall not enter my rest.”
A psalm of David, at the time when the temple was built.
Praise the Lord with a new hymn; praise the Lord, all the earth.
Praise the Lord and praise his name; proclaim the good news of his salvation day after day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all peoples.
The Lord is great and greatly praised; he is to be feared above all idols.
All the idols of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens.
Praise and beauty are before him; holiness and majesty are in his sanctuary.
Give to the Lord, families of the nations; give to the Lord glory and honor.
Give to the Lord the glory of his name; bring offerings and enter his courts.
Bow down to the Lord in the courts of his sanctuary; let all the earth tremble before him.
Say among the nations, “The Lord reigns. He established the world so that it will not be shaken, and he will judge his peoples fairly.”
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let the sea rejoice with all that fills it.
Let the fields rejoice, and everything in them; then let all the trees of the forest rejoice.
Before the Lord, for he comes—he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with justice and all the peoples with his truth.
A psalm of David, at the time when the earth was established.
The Lord reigns; let the earth be glad, and let the many islands rejoice.
Clouds and darkness surround him; his throne is established in justice and righteousness.
Fire will go before him and burn up his enemies all around.
His lightning appeared to the world; the earth saw it and trembled.
The mountains will melt like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens will proclaim his righteousness, and all the peoples will see his glory.
Let all who worship idols and boast in their carved images be ashamed. Let all his angels worship him.
Zion heard and rejoiced, and the daughters of Judah will be glad because of your judgments, Lord.
For you are exalted above all the earth; you are raised far above all idols.
You who love the Lord, hate evil. The Lord guards the lives of his holy ones; he will rescue them from the hands of the sinner.
Light dawned for the righteous, and joy came to the upright in heart.
Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
A psalm of David.
Praise the Lord with a new song of praise, for he has done wonders. His right hand and his holy arm saved him.
The Lord showed his salvation; he revealed his righteousness before the nations.
He remembered his mercy toward Jacob and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel, and all the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God.
Shout to the Lord, all the earth; praise, rejoice, and sing psalms.
Sing psalms to our God with praise, with praise and the sound of psalms.
With the sound of praise from a hammered trumpet, with praise and rejoicing, and with the sound of a horn trumpet, shout before the King, the Lord.
Let the sea roar with all that fills it, the world and all its inhabitants.
And let the rivers clap their hands together; let the mountains rejoice.
Before the Lord, for he is coming, and the Lord has arrived to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and his peoples with uprightness.
A psalm of David.
The Lord reigns; the peoples are angry. He sits upon the cherubim; the earth trembles.
The Lord is great in Zion and exalted above all peoples.
Let them praise your great name, for it is fearsome and holy.
The king’s honor loves justice. You established uprightness; you carried out justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the Lord our God; bow down at his footstool, for he is holy.
Moses and Aaron were his priests, and Samuel was among those who called upon his name. They called upon the Lord, and he heard them.
And he spoke to them in a pillar of cloud. They kept his testimonies and the commands he gave them.
Lord our God, you heard them. You were a forgiving God to them, yet you took vengeance for all their deeds.
Exalt the Lord our God; bow down at his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.
A psalm of thanksgiving, of David.
Shout to the Lord, all the earth.
Serve the Lord with gladness; enter his presence with rejoicing. Know that he is the Lord our God. He made us, and not we ourselves. We are his people and the flock of his pasture.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. Give thanks to the Lord and bless his name.
The Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting, and his faithfulness endures from generation to generation.
A psalm of David.
I will praise you for mercy and justice, Lord; I will sing a psalm.
And I will consider the blameless way until he comes to me, for I walked with a blameless heart within my house.
I set no unjust thing before my eyes. I hated those who practiced apostasy; it did not come near me.
The one whose heart was crooked turned away from me; I paid no attention to the foolish person.
I drove away the one who secretly spoke against his neighbor. I would not even eat bread with the one whose eyes were haughty and whose heart was greedy.
My eyes were upon the faithful of the land, so that they might sit with me. The one who walked in a blameless way served me.
The one who acted arrogantly did not dwell within my house. The one who spoke lawlessness did not prosper before my eyes.
Each morning I killed all the sinners of the land, so that I might destroy from the Lord’s city all those who practice lawlessness.
A prayer of a poor man when he grows weary and pours out his requests before the Lord.
Lord, hear my prayer; let my cry come to you.
Do not turn your face away from me in the day of my distress. Incline your ear to me; on the day I call to you, hear me quickly.
My days have vanished like smoke, and my bones have dried up like brushwood.
My heart has been struck down like grass and has withered; I have forgotten to eat my bread.
Because of the sound of my groaning, my bones cling to my flesh.
I have become like a pelican in the wilderness; I have become like an owl among ruins.
I have stayed awake and become like a sparrow alone on a rooftop.
My enemies reproached me all day long, and those who praise me swear by me.
I ate ashes like bread and mixed my drink with tears,
because of your anger and wrath, for you lifted me up and brought me low.
My days passed away like a shadow, and I withered like grass.
But you, Lord, remain forever, and your remembrance endures from generation to generation.
You will arise and have mercy on Zion; the time to have mercy on her has come.
Your servants take pleasure in her stones and will have compassion on her dust.
The nations will fear your name, and all the kings of the earth your glory.
The Lord builds Zion and will appear in it in his glory.
He looked upon the prayer of the lowly and did not despise their requests.
Let this be written for another generation, and let the people he has made his own praise the Lord.
He looked down from the heights, from his holy place; the Lord looked from heaven upon the earth,
to hear the groaning of prisoners and to release the children of those condemned to death,
to proclaim the Lord’s name in Zion and his praises in Jerusalem,
when peoples gather together, and kings gather to serve the Lord.
He answered him on the way of his strength: “Tell me the shortness of my days,
and do not take me away in the middle of my days, for your years endure from generation to generation.”
In the beginning, Lord, you established the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will pass away, but you endure and remain forever. They will all wear out like clothes; like a cloak you will change them, and they will be changed.
But you are the same, and your years will not pass away.
The children of your servants will dwell in it, and their offspring will prosper forever.
A psalm of David.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and all my bones, bless his holy name.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and do not forget all his gifts.
He forgives your sins and heals all your diseases.
He redeems your life from destruction and crowns you with mercy and compassion.
He satisfies your desire with good things; your youth will be renewed like an eagle’s.
The Lord shows mercy and grants justice to all who are oppressed.
The Lord made his ways known to Moses and his will to the children of Israel.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.
The Lord will not remain angry forever, nor will he hold a grudge eternally.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our lawlessness.
Rather, as the heavens are high above the earth, so the Lord has made his mercy great toward those who fear him.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our lawless deeds from us.
As a father has compassion on his children, so the Lord will have compassion on those who fear him.
For he knew how we were formed and remembered that we are dust.
A person’s days are like grass; like a flower of the field, he blooms.
The wind blows over it, and it is gone, and its place is no longer seen.
But the Lord’s mercy is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear him, and his righteousness extends to their children’s children.
They keep his covenant, remember his commandments, and carry them out.
The Lord has established his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over all.
Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who carry out his word when you hear the voice of his commands.
Bless the Lord, all his hosts, his servants who carry out his will.
Bless the Lord, all his works, in every place under his dominion. Bless the Lord, my soul.
A psalm of David about the works of creation.
Bless the Lord, my soul. O Lord my God, you are exceedingly great; you have clothed yourself in praise and majesty.
You wrapped yourself in light as in a garment; you stretched out the heavens like a tent.
And you set its upper chambers upon the waters. He makes the clouds his paths and travels upon the wings of the winds.
He made his angels spirits and his servants a burning fire.
He established the earth upon its foundation, so that it should never be shaken.
The deep covers it like a garment; the waters will stand above the mountains.
At your rebuke they will flee, and at the sound of your thunder they will tremble.
They rise into mountains and descend into plains, to the place where you established them.
You set a boundary that they do not cross, and they do not return again to cover the earth.
You sent springs through the ravines; the waters will flow between the mountains,
to give drink to all the wild beasts. The wild donkeys will quench their thirst.
There the birds of the sky will make their nests, and from among the rocks they will give their calls.
He waters the mountains from his storehouses; the earth will be filled with the fruit of his works.
You made grass grow for livestock and green plants for human use; you brought bread out of the earth.
Wine brings joy, oil brings cheer, and bread strengthens the human heart.
The trees of the Lord will be satisfied, and the cedars of Lebanon that you planted.
There the birds of the sky will hatch their young, and the stork's nest is their refuge.
The high mountains are for the deer, and the rocks are a refuge for the hares.
You made the moon to mark time; the sun knew the hour of its setting.
You made darkness, and it became night; in it all the beasts of the forest roam.
The young lions roar and seize their prey, and they seek their food from God.
When the sun rises, they gather together and rest in their thickets.
A person goes out to work and to the labor of their hands until evening.
How great are your works, Lord! You made everything with wisdom, and the earth was filled with your creatures.
This sea is great and calm; in it are creatures without number, beasts both large and small.
In it ships also sail, and the dragon that you created to play with.
They all wait for you, and you give them their food at the proper time.
You give to them, and they are fed. You open your hand and feed them all according to your will.
You turn your face away from them, and they are troubled. You take their spirit away from them, and they perish and return to dust.
You send your spirit and create them, and you renew the face of the earth.
May the glory of the Lord endure forever; may the Lord rejoice in his creatures.
He looks at the earth and makes it tremble; he draws near to the mountains, and they smoke.
I will praise the Lord throughout my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I live.
May my praise be pleasing to him, and I will rejoice in the Lord.
May sinners perish from the earth, and may the ungodly no longer be found on it. Bless the Lord, my soul. Hallelujah!
Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name; proclaim his deeds among the nations.
Praise him and sing psalms to him; tell of all his wonders.
And glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
Seek the Lord and be strong, and seek his face at all times.
Remember the wonders he performed, his mighty deeds, and the judgments of his mouth.
Descendants of Abraham, his servants; children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He himself is the Lord our God; his judgments are throughout the earth.
He has remembered his covenant forever, and the word he commanded for a thousand years.
The covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
He established his command for Jacob, and his everlasting covenant for Israel.
He says, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the allotted portion of your inheritance.”
For they were few in number, very few, and strangers in it.
They passed from nation to nation, from a kingdom to another people.
He did not allow anyone to wrong them; he rebuked kings for their sake.
He says, “Do not come near my anointed ones, and do not wrong my prophets.”
