He called down famine upon their land; he broke all the sustaining power of bread.
He sent a man ahead of them: Joseph was sold into slavery.
They brought his feet low in chains, and his body was put in irons.
Until his word came to pass, the word of the Lord tested him.
The king sent and released him; the ruler of the people set him free.
He made him lord of his household and ruler over all his possessions,
to instruct their rulers to be like himself and to make their elders wise.
Israel entered Egypt; Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
He greatly increased his people and made them stronger than their enemies.
He turned their hearts to hate his people and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
He sent Moses his servant and Aaron his chosen one.
He gave them the word of his signs and his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness and darkened them, because they rebelled against his word.
He turned their rivers into blood and killed all their fish.
Their land teemed with frogs, even in the storehouses of their kings.
He spoke, and biting flies and gnats came throughout all their territory.
He turned their rains into hail, and fire blazed in their land.
He struck their vineyards and fig trees and shattered all the trees in their territory.
He spoke, and locusts and caterpillars came, beyond counting.
It ate all the grass of their land and consumed all the fruit of their fields.
He struck all the firstborn of the Egyptians, the first fruits of all their labor.
He brought them out with gold and silver, and there was no one sick among their people.
Egypt rejoiced at their departure, for the fear of the Lord had fallen upon them.
He spread out a cloud to shade them by day, and with fire he gave them light at night.
They asked, and quail came, and he filled them with bread from heaven.
He struck the rock, and water gushed out, and rivers flowed through the dry places.
He remembered his holy word to Abraham his servant.
He brought out his people with rejoicing and his chosen ones with gladness.
He gave them the lands of the nations and made them inherit the fruits of the peoples’ labor,
so that they would keep his testimonies and seek his laws.
Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Who can tell of the Lord’s mighty deeds and make all his praises heard?
Blessed are those who uphold justice and do what is right at all times.
Remember us, Lord, with the favor you show your people, and visit us with your salvation.
May we see the goodness of your chosen ones, rejoice in the joy of your nation, and glory in your inheritance.
We have sinned along with our ancestors; we have acted lawlessly and done wrong.
Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand your wonders or remember your many mercies. They angered you as they passed through the Red Sea.
He saved them for the sake of his name, so that they might know his mighty deeds.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up. He led them through the depths as through a wilderness.
He rescued them from the hands of those who hated them and saved them from the hands of their enemies.
The sea covered their oppressors, and not one of them survived.
They believed his word and sang his praise.
They quickly forgot his deeds and did not heed his counsel.
They craved intensely in the wilderness and put God to the test in the waterless land.
He gave them what they requested and sent fullness into their souls.
They provoked Moses in the camp, and Aaron, the Lord’s holy one.
The earth opened and swallowed Dathan and covered Abiram’s company.
A fire blazed in their assembly, and a flame consumed the sinners.
They made a calf at Horeb and bowed down to an image.
And they exchanged their glory for the likeness of a calf that eats grass.
They forgot God, their savior, who performed his great deeds in Egypt,
his wonders in the land of Ham, and his acts of terror upon the Red Sea.
He said he would destroy them, had not Moses, his chosen one, stood before him. Moses turned to the Lord and turned away his anger so that they would not be destroyed.
They despised the desirable land and did not believe his word.
They grumbled in their camps and did not listen to the Lord’s voice.
He raised his hand against them to strike them in the wilderness.
May their offspring be scattered among the nations; may their offspring be scattered throughout the lands.
They defiled themselves at Baal-peor; they ate what had been sacrificed and dead flesh.
They provoked him to anger by their deeds, and destruction repeatedly fell upon them.
Then Phinehas stood among them and made atonement, and death was stopped.
It was counted to him as righteousness, from generation to generation forever.
They provoked him to anger at the waters of strife, and Moses suffered because of them.
Because they embittered his spirit, he murmured with his lips.
And they did not destroy the nations as the Lord had told them.
They mingled with the Gentiles and learned their practices.
They served their idols, and this became a stumbling block to them.
They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons and shed innocent blood.
The blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan—the land was stained with their blood.
And it was defiled by their deeds, for they prostituted themselves in their conduct.
The Lord became fiercely angry with his people and utterly abhorred his inheritance.
He delivered them into the hands of the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
And their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought low under their hands.
Many times he rescued them, but they embittered him with their schemes and were brought low by their lawlessness.
The Lord looked upon their afflictions when he heard the sound of their prayers.
He remembered his covenant and relented according to his abundant mercy.
He caused all their captors to show them compassion.
Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the Gentiles, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, forever and ever. And let all the people say, “So be it, so be it.”
Hallelujah.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let those redeemed by the Lord say this, those whom he redeemed from the hand of the enemy.
He gathered them from every land, from the east and the west, from the north and the sea.
They wandered in the wilderness along a waterless road and found no city to dwell in.
They hungered and thirsted, and their souls fainted within them.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
He led them along a straight path, so that they might go to a city where they could dwell.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for the children of men.
For he satisfied the hungry souls and filled the needy souls with good things.
Those who sat in darkness and in the shadow of death were bound in poverty as in iron chains.
For they rebelled against the word of God and rejected the counsel of the Most High.
They were brought low by suffering; their hearts grew weak, and there was no one to help them.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he brought them out of their troubles.
He rescued them from darkness and the shadow of death and broke their bonds.
Let them thank the Lord for his mercy and for his wonderful deeds for humankind.
For he shattered the bronze gates and broke the iron bars.
He helped them on the path of their lawlessness, for they were brought very low because of their sins.
Their hearts loathed every kind of food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
He sent his word and healed them and rescued them from their destruction.
Let them thank the Lord for his mercy and for his wonderful deeds for humankind.
Let them offer him a sacrifice of praise and recount his deeds with rejoicing.
Those who went down to the sea in ships and carried on their work on the vast waters.
They saw the Lord's deeds and his wonders in the depths of the abyss.
He spoke, and a wind and a storm arose, and its waves rose high.
They rose to the heavens and descended into the depths, and their souls wasted away within them.
They were troubled and staggered like drunken people, and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
He turned the storm into a breeze, and its waves grew still.
They rejoiced because the waves grew still, and he guided them to the harbor they desired.
Let them thank the Lord for his mercy and for his wonderful deeds for humankind.
Let them exalt him in the assemblies of the peoples and praise him in the councils of the elders.
He turned rivers into dry ground and streams of water into thirsty land.
He made fruitful land into salt flats because of the wickedness of its inhabitants.
He made the wilderness into pools of water and thirsty land into streams of water.
He settled the hungry there, and they built a city to live in.
They plowed fields and planted vineyards and produced their harvests of grain.
He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly, and their livestock did not decrease.
They dwindled in number and suffered from the oppression of evils and from sorrows.
Contempt came upon their rulers; he made them wander in the wilderness, where there was no road.
He helped the needy in their poverty and led their families like a flock.
The upright will see and rejoice, and every lawless person will shut his mouth.
Who is wise enough to observe these things and understand the mercies of the Lord?
Praise. Psalms of David.
My heart is ready, O God; my heart is ready to praise you and sing psalms to you with my glory.
Awake, my glory; awake with psalms and praise, and I will awake at dawn.
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, Lord, and sing psalms to you among the nations.
Your mercy has grown great as far as the heavens, and your truth reaches the clouds.
You are exalted in the heavens, O God, and your glory is throughout the earth.
As your beloved were delivered, save with your right hand and hear us.
God spoke from his holiness: “I will be exalted; I will divide Shechem and measure out the valleys of tents.”
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the strength of my head; Judah is my king.
Moab is the basin of my hope; toward Edom I will direct my steps, and foreigners have submitted to me.
Who will bring me into the fortified city, or who will lead me as far as Edom?
Is it not you, O God, who rejected us and did not go out with our armies, O God?
Give us help in distress, for human deliverance is vain.
With God we will act mightily, and he will put our enemies to shame.
For the end. A psalm of David.
O God of my praise, do not be silent, for the mouth of a sinner and the mouth of a deceitful person have opened against me; they have spoken about me with a deceitful tongue.
They surrounded me with words of hatred and fought against me without cause.
In return for my love they betrayed me, but I remained in prayer.
They repaid me with evil for good, and with hatred for my love.
Set a sinner over him; let Satan stand at his right hand.
Let him come out of his trial condemned, and let his prayers be counted as sins.
Let his days be few, and let another take his office.
Let his children be orphans and his wife a widow.
May his children wander and move about; may they become beggars and leave their dwelling.
May a creditor search out all his possessions, and may strangers seize the fruits of his labor.
May no one be found to help him, and may no one have mercy on his orphans.
May his children be destroyed, and may his name be erased from his family line.
May his father's sins be remembered before the Lord, and may his mother's sins not be erased.
May they remain before the Lord at all times, and may their memory be destroyed from the earth.
Because he did not remember to show mercy, but persecuted the poor and needy man, seeking to kill the one who was humble in heart.
He loved cursing, so may it come upon him; he did not desire blessing, so may it be far from him.
He clothed himself in cursing like a garment; may it enter his belly like water and his bones like oil.
May it be to him like a garment he wears, like a belt that is always wrapped around his waist.
This is the work of those who accused me before the Lord and who spoke evil of my soul.
But you, Lord, Lord, deal with me according to your name, for your mercy is sweet, and deliver me.
For I am poor and needy, and my heart is troubled within me.
Like a shadow, I faded as I slipped away, and I was shaken off like a locust.
My knees grew weak from fasting, and my flesh changed for lack of oil.
I became an object of reproach to them; they saw me and shook their heads.
Help me, Lord my God, and save me according to your mercy.
Let them know that this is your hand and that you, Lord, have done this.
They curse, but you will bless. May those who have risen against me be put to shame, but may your servant rejoice in you.
May those who accused my soul be clothed in shame, and may they wrap their shame around themselves like a cloak.
But I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth; in the midst of many people I will bless you.
For he stood at the right hand of the needy one, to save me from those who persecute my soul.
For the end. A psalm of David.
The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”
The Lord will send you a scepter of power from Zion, and you will rule in the midst of your enemies.
With you is, for me, the beginning of the days of power, in the splendor of your holy ones. From the womb, before the morning star, I begot you.
The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
And the Lord at your right hand will crush kings on the day of his wrath.
He will judge the nations and inflict many blows, and he will crush the heads of many on the earth.
He will drink [?] along the way; therefore he will also lift up the heads.
Hallelujah.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart, in the council of the upright, in the congregation.
Great are the works of the Lord, and his purposes have been examined in every respect.
His works are praise and splendor; his righteousness endures forever and ever.
He made a memorial of his wonders for the upright. The Lord is merciful and compassionate.
He gives food to those who fear him; he has remembered his covenant forever.
He made known the power of his works to his people, giving them the inheritance of the nations.
And the works of his hands are righteousness and justice; all his commandments are trustworthy.
They are established forever and ever, carried out in truth and uprightness.
The Lord sent redemption to his people; he ordained his covenant forever. Holy and fearsome is his name.
The beginning of prudence is the fear of the Lord. All who practice it have good understanding, and his praise endures forever and ever.
Hallelujah.
Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly desires his commandments.
His offspring will be mighty on the earth, and the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Glory and greatness are in his house; his righteousness endures forever and ever.
Light has dawned in the darkness for the upright. The Lord is merciful, compassionate, and righteous.
A kind man shows mercy and lends; he orders his affairs with justice.
For he will never be shaken; the righteous man will be remembered forever.
He will not fear bad news; his heart is ready to trust in God.
His heart is steadfast, and he will not fear until he looks upon his enemies.
He distributed and gave to the poor; his righteousness endures forever and ever, and his horn will be raised in glory.
The sinner will see and become angry; he will gnash his teeth and waste away, and the desire of sinners will perish.
Hallelujah.
Praise the Lord, you servants, and praise the name of the Lord.
May the name of the Lord be blessed from now on and forever.
From sunrise to sunset, the name of the Lord is blessed.
The Lord is exalted above all nations, and his glory is in the heavens.
Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high
and sees the lowly in heaven and on earth?
He raises the poor from the earth and lifts the afflicted from the dung heaps.
He seats them as princes among the princes of his people.
He settles the barren woman in a home, joyful like a mother rejoicing in her children.
Hallelujah.
When Israel came out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of another nation,
Judea became his sanctuary, and Israel his dominion.
The sea saw and fled, and the Jordan turned back.
The mountains leaped like rams, and the hills like lambs of the flock.
What is the matter with you, sea? Whom did you see that you fled? Or you, Jordan, why did you turn back?
Mountains, leap like rams, and hills, like lambs of the flock.
The earth trembled before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
who turned the rock into streams of water and the flint into springs.
Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, because of your mercy and your truth.
May they never say among the nations, “Where is their God?”
Our God is in heaven and on earth; he has done everything he wished.
The idols of the nations are gold and silver, made by human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.
They have ears but do not hear; they have noses but do not smell.
They have hands but do not feel; they have feet but do not walk, and there is no voice in their throats.
May those who made them become like them, along with everyone who trusts in them.
The house of Israel trusted in the Lord; he is their helper and support.
The house of Aaron trusted in the Lord; he is their helper and companion.
Those who fear the Lord trusted in the Lord; he is their helper and deliverer.
The Lord remembered us and blessed us. The Lord blessed the house of Israel; the Lord blessed the house of Aaron.
The Lord blessed those who fear him, both small and great.
May the Lord increase you, you and your children.
You are blessed by the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
The heavens of heavens belong to the Lord, but he gave the earth to the children of humankind.
The dead will not bless you, Lord, nor will any who descend into the realm of the dead.
But we who are living will bless the Lord from now on and forever.
Hallelujah.
I have loved, because the Lord will hear the voice of my prayers.
For he inclined his ear to me, and throughout my days I called upon him.
The pangs of death surrounded me, and the pains of the realm of the dead found me; I found distress and anguish.
And I called upon the name of the Lord: “O Lord, save my soul!”
The Lord our God is merciful and righteous.
He has mercy, and the Lord protects children. I was brought low, and the Lord saved me.
Return, my soul, to your rest, for the Lord has helped you.
He delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling.
I will be pleasing before the Lord in the land of the living.
Hallelujah.
I believed, and therefore I spoke; and I was brought very low.
I said in my astonishment, “Every person is a liar.”
What shall I give the Lord in return for all that he has given me?
I will take the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord.
I will offer my prayers to the Lord before all his people.
Precious before the Lord is the death of his holy ones.
O Lord, I am your servant, a servant and the son of your maidservant. You have broken my bonds.
I will offer you a sacrifice of praise and call upon the name of the Lord.
I will offer my prayers to the Lord before all his people.
In the courts of the Lord’s house and in your midst, Jerusalem.
Hallelujah.
Praise the Lord, all nations; praise him, all peoples.
May his mercy prevail over us, and may the Lord’s truth endure forever.
Hallelujah.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let the house of Israel say that he is good, that his mercy endures forever.
Let the house of Aaron say that he is good, that his mercy endures forever.
Let those who fear the Lord say that he is good, that his mercy endures forever.
In my distress I called to the Lord, and he answered me with relief.
The Lord is my helper, and I will not be afraid. What can a person do to me?
The Lord is my helper, and I will look upon my enemies.
It is better to trust in the Lord than to trust in people.
It is better to trust in the Lord than to trust in rulers.
All nations surrounded me, and in the Lord’s name I defeated them.
They surrounded me on every side and together besieged me, and in the Lord’s name I drove them away.
They surrounded me like bees; they burned and blazed like thorns in a fire, and in the Lord’s name I repelled them.
When I was pushed back, I staggered and nearly fell, but the Lord upheld me.
The Lord is my strength and my help, and he became my salvation.
The sound of rejoicing and salvation is in the dwellings of the righteous. The Lord’s right hand has done mighty deeds.
The Lord’s right hand lifted me high, and the Lord’s right hand has done mighty deeds.
I will not die but live, and I will recount the Lord’s works.
The Lord disciplined me severely, but he did not hand me over to death.
Open for me the gates of righteousness, so that I may enter through them and give thanks to the Lord.
This is the Lord’s gate, and the righteous enter through it.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, because you heard me and became my salvation.
The stone that the builders rejected became the cornerstone.
This came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day that the Lord made. Come, let us rejoice and be glad in it.
O Lord, save us! O Lord, guide us!
Blessed are you who come in the name of the Lord. We have blessed you from the house of the Lord.
The Lord our God appeared to us. Celebrate joyful festivals early, as far as the corners of the altar.
You are my God, and I will give thanks to you. You are my God, and I will exalt you. I will give thanks to you, Lord, because you heard me and became my salvation.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.
Hallelujah.
Blessed are those who are blameless in their way and who walk according to the law of the Lord.
Blessed are those who examine his testimonies; they will seek him with their whole heart.
Those who practice lawlessness will not walk in his ways.
You commanded me to keep your commandments diligently.
Oh, that my ways were directed toward keeping your statutes!
Then I would not be ashamed when I paid heed to your commandments.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, with an upright heart, as I learn your righteous judgments.
I have kept your ordinances; do not abandon me completely.
How can a young man straighten his ways, except by keeping your words?
With my whole heart I have sought you; do not cast me away from your commandments.
I hid your words in my heart so that I would not sin against you.
Blessed are you, Lord; teach me your statutes.
With my lips I will recount all the ordinances of your mouth.
I rejoiced in the way of your testimonies as in all riches.
I reflected on your commandments and paid heed to your ways.
I spoke of your judgments and did not forget your words.
Deal generously with your servant, so that I may live and keep your words.
Open my eyes, and I will look upon the wonders of your law.
I am a stranger on the earth; do not hide your commandments from me.
My soul yearned with longing for your judgments at all times.
You rebuked the proud, the accursed who turned away from your commandments.
Remove reproach and contempt from me, for I sought your testimonies.
For rulers sat and spoke evil of me, but your servant pondered your ordinances.
For your testimonies were my words, and your righteousness was my counsel.
My soul drew near to the dust. Lord, keep me alive according to your word.
I told you of my ways, and you heard me. Teach me your statutes.
Give me understanding of the ways of your statutes, and I will examine your wonders.
My soul labored to the point of weariness; strengthen me with your words.
Remove the way of sin from me, and show me mercy through your law.
I have chosen the paths of your truth, and I have not forgotten your ordinances.
I drew near to your testimonies. Lord, do not put me to shame.
I ran in the way of your commandments, for you gave my heart ease.
Make me knowledgeable, Lord, in the way of your decrees, and I will seek it at all times.
Give me understanding, and I will examine your law and keep it with all my heart.
Lead me in the paths of your commandments, for I delighted in them.
Incline my heart toward your testimonies and not toward greed.
Turn my eyes away so that I do not see vanity; keep me alive in your ways.
Establish your word for your servant in the fear of you.
Take away from me the reproach that I anticipated, for your judgments are good.
See, I have longed for your commandments; in your righteousness preserve my life.
May your mercy come upon me, Lord, and your salvation according to your word.
I will answer those who reproach me with words, for I have put my hope in your words.
Do not utterly take the word of truth from my mouth, for I have put my hope in your judgments.
I kept your law at all times, forever and for ever and ever.
I walked at ease, for I sought your commandments.
I spoke of your testimonies before kings and was not ashamed.
I meditated on your commandments, which I loved.
I lifted my hands toward your commandments, which I loved, and meditated on your righteousness.
Remember the word to your servant, in which you made me hope.
This will comfort me in my humiliation, because your words gave me life.
The proud treated me very unjustly, but I did not turn aside from your laws.
I remembered your judgments from of old, Lord, and was comforted.
Sorrow seized me because of the sinners who abandoned your laws.
Your judgments are praiseworthy to me in the place where I live as a stranger.
I remembered your name in the night, Lord, and kept your laws.
This became a path to life for me, because I sought your statutes.
You are my portion, Lord; I said that I would keep your laws.
I sought your favor with all my heart; have mercy on me according to your word.
I considered my ways and turned my feet toward your testimonies.
I made myself ready and was not troubled, because I kept your commandments.
The nets of sin surrounded me, but I did not forget your laws.
In the middle of the night I would rise to give thanks to you for your righteous judgments.
I was a companion of all who fear you, who have kept your commandments.
The earth is filled with the Lord's mercy; teach me your statutes.
You have dealt kindly with your servant, Lord, according to your word.
Teach me goodness, discipline, and knowledge, because I believed in your commandments.
Before I was humbled, I sinned; therefore I kept your words diligently.
You are kind, Lord, and in your kindness teach me your statutes.
The injustices of the proud against me multiplied, but I examined your commandments with all my heart.
Their heart curdled like milk, but I spoke of your laws.
It is good for me that you humbled me, so that I might learn your statutes.
The laws of your mouth are better for me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.
Your hands made me and formed me. Make me wise, and I will learn your commandments.
Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, because I have hoped in your words.
I know, Lord, that your judgments are righteous, and that you have rightly humbled me.
Let your mercy comfort me, according to your word to your servant.
Let your compassion come to me, and I will live, for your law was my meditation.
Let the proud be ashamed, for they wronged me without cause; but I will meditate on your commandments.
Let those who fear you instruct me, along with those who know your testimonies.
Let my heart be blameless in your righteousness, so that I may not be put to shame.
My soul longed for your salvation, for I have hoped in your words.
My eyes waited for your word. I said, “When will you comfort me?”
I became like a wineskin in the frost, for I did not forget your statutes.
How many are the days of your servant? When will you give me justice against my persecutors?
The lawless told me of their counsels, but not according to your law.
All your commandments are true. They persecuted me without cause; help me.
They almost destroyed me on earth, but I did not abandon your commandments.
Keep me alive according to your mercy, and I will keep the testimonies of your mouth.
Forever, Lord, your word stands in heaven.
Your faithfulness lasts from generation to generation. You established the earth, and it stands.
The day remains by your command, for all things are your servants.
If your law had not been my meditation, I would already have perished long ago in my humiliation.
I will never forget your statutes, for through them you kept me alive.
I am yours; keep me alive, for I have sought your statutes.
Sinners lay in wait for me to destroy me, for I took your testimonies to heart.
I saw an end to every perfection; your commandments were a great comfort to me.
How I loved your law! It was my meditation all day long.
Through your commandments you made me wiser than my enemies, for they were mine forever.
I became wiser than all my teachers, for your testimonies were my discourse.
I became wiser than the elders, for I examined your commandments.
I kept my feet from every evil path so that I might keep your words.
I did not turn aside from your judgments, for you taught me your law.
How sweet your words are to my palate, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
Through your commandments I gained understanding and hated every evil path, for you made me knowledgeable in the law.
Your words are a lamp for my feet and give light to my paths.
I swore and confirmed that I would keep all your righteous judgments.
I have been brought very low. Lord, give me life according to your word.
Lord, accept the freewill offerings of my mouth, and teach me your judgments.
My life is in your hands at all times, and I have not forgotten your law.
Sinners set a snare for me, but I did not stray from your commandments.
I have inherited your testimonies forever, for they are the joy of my heart.
I inclined my heart to carry out your righteous statutes forever, for the sake of the reward.
I hated the lawless and loved your law.
You are my helper and deliverer, and I have put my hope in your words.
Depart from me, you evildoers, and I will examine the commandments of my God.
Help me according to your word and give me life, and do not put me to shame in my hope.
Help me and save me, and I will meditate on your judgments at all times.
You despised all who rebelled against your righteous statutes, for their thoughts were unjust.
I counted all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore I loved your commandments.
Nail my flesh with fear of you, for I greatly feared your judgments.
I have done what is just and righteous; do not hand me over to my oppressors.
Accept your servant for good, so that the proud may not harass me.
My eyes have waited for your salvation, Lord, and for the words of your righteousness.
Deal with your servant according to your mercy; teach me your righteous statutes.
I am your servant; make me wise, and I will know your testimonies.
It is time for the Lord to arise; they have made your law void.
Therefore I loved your commandments more than all gold and topaz.
All your commandments have worked for my good, for I have hated the ways of the wicked.
Your testimonies are wonderful; therefore my soul has loved them.
The revelation of your words gives light and makes the young wise.
I opened my mouth and drew breath; my soul longed for your commandments.
Look upon me and have mercy on me, as is right for those who love your name.
Make my paths straight according to your word, and let no sin rule over me.
Deliver me from human slander, and I will keep your commandments.
Show your face to your servant, and teach me your righteous ordinances.
Streams of water flowed from my eyes because they did not keep your law.
You are righteous, Lord, and your judgments are upright.
You have commanded righteousness in your testimonies, and they are utterly true.
Zeal for you has consumed me, because my enemies have forgotten your words.
Your words are thoroughly refined, and your servant has loved them.
I am young and despised, but I have not forgotten your righteous ordinances.
Your righteousness is everlasting righteousness, and your laws are true.
Trouble and distress found me, but your commandments were my meditation.
Your testimonies are righteous forever; make me wise and keep me alive.
I called to you with my whole heart; hear me, Lord, for I have sought your righteous decrees.
I cried out to you: deliver me, and I will keep your testimonies.
I rose before the appointed hour and cried out, and I placed my hope in your words.
My eyes were awake before dawn, so that I might meditate on your words.
Hear my voice, Lord, according to your mercy; Lord, keep me alive according to your judgments.
My persecutors brought lawlessness near me, for they were far from your laws.
You are near, Lord, and all your commandments are true.
From the beginning I knew from your testimonies that you had established them forever.
See my lowly condition and deliver me, for I have not forgotten your law.
Plead my case and deliver me, and preserve my life according to your word.
Salvation is far from sinners, because they have not kept your judgments.
Your mercies are many, Lord; give me life according to your judgments.
Many persecute and oppress me, but I have not strayed from your testimonies.
I looked at the wicked and wasted away, because they did not keep your commandments.
See how I have loved your commandments, Lord; give me life through your mercy.
The beginning of your words is truth, and all your righteous judgments last forever.
Rulers persecuted me without cause, and my heart stood in fear of your words.
I rejoiced in your words like someone who finds abundant spoils.
I hated and despised sins, and I loved your law.
Seven times a day I will praise you for your righteous judgments.
Those who love your law have great peace, and nothing causes them to stumble.
I waited for your salvation, Lord, and loved your commandments.
My soul kept your testimonies and loved them greatly.
I kept your commandments and your testimonies, because all my ways are before you.
Let my petitions come before you, Lord; make me wise according to your word.
Let my prayers come before you, Lord, and save me by your word.
My lips will pour forth your praises when you teach me your righteous decrees.
Let my tongue speak your words, because all your commandments are righteous.
Let your hand give me life, because I have chosen your commandments.
I longed for your salvation, Lord, and your law was my meditation.
Let my soul live and praise you, and let your judgments help me.
I have wandered like a lost sheep; seek your servant, because I have not forgotten your commandments.
Songs of Ascents
In my distress I called to the Lord, and he heard me.
Lord, save my soul from deceitful lips and an evil tongue.
What will be given to you, or what will be added to you, deceitful tongue?
Like a mighty warrior's arrows, for they are tempered with glowing coals of oak.
Woe to me, because my stay in a foreign land has grown long! I lived in the tents of Kedar.
My soul has often lived among those who hated peace.
I was a peacemaker; when I spoke, they fought against me.
Blessings of Ascents
I lifted my eyes to the mountains, from where help will come to me.
My help will come from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
Do not let your foot slip, and may your guardian not slumber.
How the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor goes to sleep!
May the Lord guard you, and may the Lord uphold you with his right hand.
May the sun not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.
May the Lord guard you from every evil; may the Lord guard your soul.
May the Lord guard your coming in and your going out, from now until forever.
Blessings of Ascents
I rejoiced when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the Lord.”
Our feet had arrived and were standing at your gates, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is built as a city, with its habitation around it.
There the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, the testimonies of Israel, to give thanks to the name of the Lord.
There thrones of judgment have been set, thrones set in the house of David.
Ask for the peace and prosperity of Jerusalem, you who love her.
May there be peace within your defenses and prosperity in your fortified towers.
For the sake of my brothers and companions, I spoke of peace for you.
And for the sake of the house of the Lord our God, we sought good for you.
Blessings of Ascents
To you, Lord, I lifted my eyes, you who dwell in heaven.
As the eyes of servants look to the hands of their masters, as the eyes of a maidservant look to the hands of her mistress, so our eyes look to you, Lord our God, until you have mercy on us.
Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, for we have been filled with much contempt.
Our souls have been filled still more with the insults of those who insulted us and with the contempt of the proud.
Blessings of Ascents
If the Lord had not been with us, let Israel say,
If the Lord had not been with us when people rose up against us,
they would have swallowed us alive when their furious anger flared against us.
then the waters would indeed have engulfed us; our souls would have passed through torrents.
Our souls passed through restless waters.
Blessed is the Lord, who did not give us as prey to their teeth.
Our souls escaped like a sparrow from the hunters’ snare. Their snares were broken, and we escaped.
Our help comes from the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
Songs of Ascents.
The one who trusts in the Lord is like Mount Zion. May the one who dwells in Jerusalem never be shaken.
Mountains surround it; the Lord surrounds his people from now and forever.
The Lord will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lands allotted to the righteous, and let the righteous not stretch out their hands to lawlessness.
The Lord does good to the good and to those who are upright in heart.
But the Lord carries away those who have turned aside, along with those who practice lawlessness. Peace be upon Israel.
Songs of Ascents.
When the Lord restored the captives of Zion, we were comforted.
Then our mouths were filled with laughter and our tongues with rejoicing. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things for them.”
The Lord has done great things for us, and we were glad.
Lord, restore our captives like the torrents in the south.
Those who plowed with tears will reap with rejoicing.
They went along weeping, carrying their seeds. They will come back rejoicing, bringing their harvests.
Songs of Ascents.
Unless the Lord builds the house, its builders labor in vain. Unless the Lord guards the city, its watchmen keep watch in vain.
It is in vain for you to rise early. Now rise before you have slept, you who eat the bread of sorrows, in due time, as sleep is given to his beloved.
Children are the Lord’s inheritance; his own reward is the fruit of his own womb.
Like arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of those who have been cast out.
Blessed is the one who satisfies his desire with them. Let them not be ashamed when their enemies speak with them at the gate.
Songs of Ascents.
Blessed are all who fear the Lord and walk in his ways.
You will eat the fruit of your hands’ labor. Blessed are you, and it will be well with you.
Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the corners of your house; your children are like newly planted olive trees around your table.
Thus every person who fears the Lord will be blessed.
May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
May you see your children’s children. Peace upon Israel!
Songs of praise for the ascents.
Many times they fought against me from my youth—let Israel say.
Many times they fought against me from my youth, but they did not overcome me.
Sinners struck my back; they prolonged their lawlessness.
The Lord is righteous; he breaks the necks of sinners.
May all who hate Zion be put to shame and turn back.
Let them be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it can be gathered in a handful.
From which the reaper did not fill his hand, nor the gatherer his arms.
None of those who passed by them said, “The blessing of the Lord be with you, and we bless you in the name of the Lord.”
Songs of praise for the ascents.
From the depths I cried to you, Lord. Lord, hear my voice; let your ears listen to the sound of my prayers.
If you examine my acts of lawlessness, Lord, Lord, who can stand before you?
For forgiveness comes from you; for the sake of your name I waited, Lord.
My soul waited for your word; my soul hoped in the Lord.
From the morning watch until evening.
From the morning watch Israel hoped in the Lord. Mercy comes from the Lord, and abundant redemption comes from him.
And he redeems Israel from all its afflictions.
Songs of praise for the ascents.
Lord, my heart was not exalted, and my eyes did not roam. I did not pursue great things or things too wonderful for me.
But if I humbled myself like a child weaned from its mother’s breast, and its return again to the same [?]; yet if I indeed made my soul proud, let this be the recompense of my soul.
Israel hoped in the Lord from now and forever.
Songs of praise for the ascents.
Remember, Lord, David and all his gentleness.
How he swore to the Lord and made vows to the God of Jacob:
“I will not enter my house or climb into my bed;
I will not give sleep to my eyes, slumber to my eyelids, or rest to my body
until I find a dwelling place for the Lord, the God of Jacob.”
Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah, and we found it in the fields of the forests.
Let us enter his dwelling places; let us bow down at the place where his feet have stood.
Arise, Lord, to your resting place, you and the ark of your holy covenant.
Let your priests be clothed in righteousness, and let your holy ones rejoice greatly.
For the sake of David, your beloved, do not turn your face away from your anointed.
The Lord swore to David in truth and did not lie to him: “I will set one of the offspring of your body on your throne.
If your sons keep my laws and my testimonies, which I will teach them, their sons will sit on your throne forever and ever.”
The Lord was pleased with Zion and chose to dwell in her.
He says, “This is my resting place forever and ever. Here I will dwell, for I am pleased with her.
I will abundantly bless her food, and I will satisfy her poor with bread.
I will clothe her priests in salvation, and her holy ones will rejoice greatly.
There I will cause a horn to spring up for David; I will prepare a lamp for my anointed.
I will clothe his enemies in shame, but my holiness will blossom upon him.”
Praises of ascents.
How good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together!
Like oil that runs down onto the head and into Aaron’s beard, and from the beard runs down onto the collars of his garment.
Like dew that falls from Hermon upon Mount Zion, there the Lord prepared the blessing and eternal life.
Praises of ascents.
Here, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord who stand in the Lord’s house and in the courts of our God at night.
Lift up your hands in holiness and bless the Lord.
May the Lord, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.
Hallelujah.
Praise the name of the Lord; praise the Lord, you servants of the Lord,
who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.
Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; sing psalms to his name, for it is sweet.
The Lord chose Jacob for himself and Israel as his inheritance.
I know that the Lord is great, and the Lord is greater than all idols.
The Lord did whatever he wished in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the depths.
He brings clouds from the ends of the earth; he made his lightning for the rain and brings winds out of his storehouses.
He struck down all the firstborn of the Egyptians, both humans and animals.
He sent his signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his forces.
He struck down many nations and killed mighty kings:
Sihon, king of the Amorites, Og, king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of the Canaanites.
He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel, his people.
Lord, your name is forever; Lord, your remembrance is from generation to generation.
The Lord judges his people and takes comfort in his servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.
They have ears but do not hear, and there is no breath in their mouths.
May those who made them become like them, along with everyone who trusts in them.
House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.
House of Levi, bless the Lord; you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord.
Blessed is the Lord from Zion, he who dwells in Jerusalem. Hallelujah!
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for his mercy is forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his mercy is forever.
He alone did great wonders, for his mercy is forever.
He made the heavens by his wisdom, for his mercy is forever.
He established the earth upon the waters, for his mercy is forever.
He alone made the great lights, for his mercy is forever.
He made the sun to rule the day, for his mercy is forever.
The moon and the stars to rule the night, for his mercy endures forever.
He struck the land of the Egyptians together with its firstborn, for his mercy endures forever.
And he brought Israel out from among them, for his mercy endures forever.
With an uplifted hand and his mighty arm, for his mercy endures forever.
He split the great sea and divided it into two parts, for his mercy endures forever.
And he brought Israel through its midst, for his mercy endures forever.
He drowned Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea, for his mercy endures forever.
He brought his people out into the wilderness, for his mercy endures forever.
He struck great kings, for his mercy endures forever.
And he killed mighty kings, for his mercy endures forever.
Sihon, king of the Amorites, for his mercy endures forever.
Og, king of Bashan, for his mercy endures forever.
He gave their land as an inheritance, for his mercy endures forever.
An inheritance to Israel his servant, for his mercy endures forever.
The Lord remembered us in our lowly state, for his mercy endures forever.
And he delivered us from the hands of our enemies, for his mercy endures forever.
He who gives food to every living creature, for his mercy endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his mercy endures forever.
A psalm of David, through Jeremiah; not indicated in the Hebrew.
By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept when we remembered Zion there.
On the willows in their midst we hung our harps.
There our captors asked us for songs of praise. Those who had taken us captive pressed us, saying, “Sing us some of Zion’s songs of praise.”
But how can we sing the Lord’s songs of praise in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget me.
Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not sing of you first, Jerusalem, at the beginning of my joy.
Remember, Lord, the sons of Edom in the days of Jerusalem, who said, “Tear it down, tear it down, right down to its foundation!”
Wretched daughter of Babylon, blessed is the one who repays you for what you have done to us.
Blessed is the one who takes your little children and dashes them against the rock.
A psalm of David.
I will praise you, Lord, with my whole heart; before the angels I will sing psalms to you.
For you have heard the words of my mouth. I will bow down toward your holy temple and praise your name for your mercy and your truth, for you have exalted your holy name above everything.
On the day when I call to you, hear me quickly, and greatly increase the strength in my soul.
All the kings of the earth will praise you, for they have heard the words of your mouth.
And they will bless your ways; great is the glory of the Lord.
The Lord is exalted; he sees the humble and recognizes the proud from afar.
Even if I walk amid troubles, you will keep me alive. Against the anger of the enemy you stretched out your hand, and your right hand saved me.
And the Lord will repay on my behalf. Lord, your mercy is eternal; do not disregard the works of your hands.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Lord, you have searched me and known me.
You know when I sit down and when I rise; you understand my thoughts from afar.
You have examined my paths and my allotted portions, and you have seen all my ways beforehand.
For there is no deceit on my tongue. Behold, you, Lord, have known
what is behind me and what is before me. You formed me and laid your hand upon me.
Your knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is overwhelming, and I cannot bear it.
Where shall I go from your Spirit, or where shall I flee from your presence?
If I ascend to heaven, you are there; if I descend to Hades, you are near even there.
If I take my wings at dawn and dwell at the farthest reaches of the sea,
even there your hand will guide me, and your right hand will hold me.
I said, “Surely darkness has covered me, or night has taken the place of the light of my delight.”
Darkness is not dark to you, and the night will be as bright as day; its darkness is like its light.
You possessed my kidneys and received me from my mother’s womb.
I will praise you, Lord, because you are fearsome and wonderful. Your works are wonderful, and my soul knows this very well.
My bones were not hidden from you, which you made in secret, and the [?] of my strength was in the lowest parts of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and all were written in your book. They wandered astray by day, and there was no one to guide them.
Your friends have become greatly honored by me, O God, and their rulers have grown very powerful.
I counted them, and they were more numerous than the sand. I awoke, and now I am with you.
If you kill the sinners, O God! Men of blood, depart from me!
In opposition and envy they will take your cities in vain.
Have I not hated those who hate you, Lord, and wasted away because of your enemies?
I hated them with complete hatred, and they became my enemies.
Test me, God, and know my heart; examine me and know my paths.
And see whether there are acts of lawlessness in my ways, and lead me along your everlasting paths.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Deliver me, Lord, from an evil person; rescue me from an unjust man.
They plotted lawlessness in their hearts; every day they prepared for war.
They sharpened their tongues like a serpent’s, and the poison of vipers is beneath their lips.
Protect me, Lord, from the hands of the sinner, and rescue me from an evil person. They plotted to hinder my steps.
The proud hid a trap for me; they stretched out cords as a snare for my feet. Around my paths they set a stumbling block for me.
I said to the Lord, “You are my God.” Listen, Lord, to the sound of my prayers.
Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation, the shelter over my head on the day of battle!
Do not hand me over, Lord, to the desire of sinners who plotted against me. Do not strike me down, so that they may never be exalted, and may their plans not be fulfilled.
Their final end—may the toil of their own lips cover them.
Cast burning coals upon them and destroy them; may they be unable to live amid their torments.
May a slanderous man not prosper on earth; may the sinful man’s own evils hunt him down to destruction.
I have learned that you, Lord, bring justice to the poor and uphold the rights of the needy.
The righteous will give thanks for your name; the upright will dwell before your face.
A psalm of David.
Lord, I called to you; hear me. Attend to the voice of my prayers when I call to you.
Let my prayers rise like incense before you, Lord, and the lifting of my hands like an evening sacrifice.
Lord, set a guard over my mouth and a secure door over my lips.
Let my heart not turn aside to words of evil, making excuses for sins with people who practice lawlessness. I will not be a companion of their chosen ones.
Let the righteous man discipline me with mercy; [?] let him rebuke me. Let the oil of a sinner not anoint my head, and let my prayers be according to his will.
Their judges were swallowed up beside the rock. They will hear my words, for they are sweet.
As a clod of earth is scattered over the ground, so shall their bones be scattered near hell.
My eyes are toward you, Lord, Lord. I have placed my hope in you; do not take my soul from me.
Keep me from the snare hidden for me, from the stumbling block of those who practice lawlessness.
Let sinners fall into his nets. I am alone until I pass through.
An instruction of David. A prayer when he was there in the cave.
With my voice I called to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.
I will pour out my prayers before the Lord and tell of my troubles before him.
When my spirit fainted within me, you, Lord, knew my paths. On the road where I was walking, a snare was hidden for me.
I looked to the right and saw that there was no one who knew me. Escape was lost to me, and there was no one who sought my life.
I cried out to you, Lord, and said, “You are my hope and my portion in the land of the living.”
Lord, attend to my prayers, for I have been brought very low. Deliver me from my persecutors, for they have become stronger than I.
Lord, bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name. Your righteous people wait for me until you repay me.
A psalm of David, at the time when his son Absalom pursued him.
Lord, hear my prayers; give ear to my petitions in your truth. Hear me in your righteousness.
Do not enter into judgment with your servant, for no mortal will be justified before you.
The enemy pursued my soul and brought my life down to the earth. He made me sit in darkness like those long dead.
My spirit grew weary within me, and my heart was troubled within me.
I remembered the days of old. I meditated on all your works; I pondered what your hands had made.
I lifted my hands to you. My soul thirsts for you like thirsty ground.
Hear me quickly, Lord, for my spirit has fainted within me. Do not turn your face away from me, lest I become like those who go down into the pit.
Let me hear your mercies in the morning, for I have put my hope in you, Lord. Show me the path I should walk, for I have lifted up my soul to you, Lord.
Deliver me from my enemies, Lord, for I have made you my refuge.
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. May your good Spirit lead me on level ground.
For your name’s sake, Lord, you will preserve my life; in your righteousness you will bring my soul out of distress.
In your mercy, destroy my enemies; bring to ruin all who oppress my soul, for I am your servant.
A psalm of David against Goliath.
Blessed is the Lord my God, who taught my hands to wage war and my fingers to fight.
He is my mercy and my refuge, my helper and my deliverer, my refuge, and I put my hope in him. He subjects the peoples to me.
Lord, what is a human being, that you have revealed yourself to him, or a son of man, that you consider him worth anything?
A human being has become like a breath, and his days have passed like a shadow.
Lord, lower the heavens and come down; draw near to the mountains, and they will smoke.
Flash your lightning and throw them into confusion; send out your arrows and scatter them.
Send your hand from on high and deliver me from many waters and from the hands of foreigners.
Their mouths have spoken empty words, and their right hand is a right hand of sin.
God, I will praise you with a new song of praise; with a ten-stringed harp I will sing a psalm to you.
He will grant salvation to our kings; he will deliver David his servant from the evil sword.
Deliver me and rescue me from the hands of foreigners, whose mouths have spoken empty words and whose right hand is a right hand of sin.
Their sons are like newly planted trees, firmly established from their youth; their daughters are adorned and embellished like a temple.
Their storehouses are full and overflow into one another; their flocks bear many young and multiply wherever they go.
Their cattle are fat; there is no breach in their fence and no outcry in their squares.
Now I will call blessed the people for whom this is so; indeed, blessed are the people whose God is the Lord.
A song of praise by David.
I exalt you, my God and my King, and I bless your name forever and forever and ever.
Every day I will bless you and praise your name forever and for ever and ever.
The Lord is great and greatly praised, and his greatness has no measure.
Generation after generation will praise your works and recount your mighty deeds.
They will speak of the great splendor of your holy glory and recount your wonders.
They will speak of your awe-inspiring power and recount your great deeds.
They will pour out the memory of your abundant goodness and rejoice in your righteousness.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abounding in mercy.
The Lord is good to everyone, and his compassion extends over all his creatures.
All your works will give thanks to you, Lord, and your holy ones will bless you.
They will speak of the glory of your kingdom and tell of your mighty deeds,
To make your power known to the children of humankind, and the glorious splendor of your kingdom.
Your kingdom is a kingdom for all ages, and your dominion lasts from generation to generation. The Lord is faithful in all his words and righteous in all his works.
The Lord supports all who stumble and raises up all who have fallen.
The eyes of everyone look to you in hope, and you give them their food at the proper time. You give it to them, and they are fed.
You open your hand and fill everyone with goodness according to your will.
The Lord is righteous in all his ways and holy in all his works.
The Lord is near to all who call upon him, to all who call upon him in truth.
The Lord fulfills the wishes of those who fear him; he hears their prayers and saves them.
The Lord guards all who love him, and the Lord destroys all sinners.
My mouth will speak the praises of the Lord. Let every living creature bless his holy name forever and for ever and ever.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah.
Bless the Lord, my soul. I will praise the Lord throughout my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I exist.
Do not put your hope in rulers or in human beings, for there is no salvation in them.
Their spirit will depart from them, and they will return to the dust; on that day all their plans will perish.
Blessed is the one whose helper is the Lord, the God of Jacob, and whose hope is in the Lord God.
Who made heaven and earth, the sea and everything in them, who preserves truth forever,
And gives justice to those who are wronged, gives bread to the hungry, and releases the prisoners—the Lord.
The Lord opens the eyes of the blind, and the Lord raises up those who have fallen. The Lord loves the righteous.
The Lord guards strangers; the Lord takes in orphans and widows, and he brings the ways of the ungodly to ruin.
The Lord will reign forever—your God, Zion—from generation to generation. Hallelujah.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah.
Praise the Lord, for psalms are good for our God; let praise be sweet.
The Lord builds Jerusalem and gathers the scattered people of Israel.
He heals broken hearts and binds up all their wounds.
He counts the multitude of stars and calls them all by name.
Great is our Lord, and great is his power; his wisdom has no limit.
The Lord receives the meek and brings the proud down to the ground.
Praise the Lord with thanksgiving; sing psalms to him with praise.
He clothed the heavens with clouds, prepared his rain for the earth, and made grass grow on the mountains, green plants for human use.
He who gives the animals their food, and the young ravens that cry to him.
The Lord did not delight in the strength of a horse, nor was he pleased with the thighs of a mighty man.
Rather, the Lord was pleased with those who fear him and with those who hope in his mercy.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah.
Praise the Lord, Jerusalem, and bless your God, Zion.
For he strengthened the bars of your gates and blessed your children within you.
He made your borders peaceful and filled you with the finest wheat.
He sends his word to the earth; his commands run swiftly.
He lays down snow like wool and scattered mist like dust.
He casts down ice like fragments; who can stand before his cold?
He sends his word and melts them; the winds will sound, and the waters will flow.
He declares his word to Jacob, his righteousness and his ordinances to Israel.
The Lord did not do this for every nation, nor did he reveal his judgments to them.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah.
Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him from the heights.
Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts.
Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all stars and light.
Praise him, heaven of heavens, and waters above the heavens.
Praise the name of the Lord, for he spoke and they came into being; he commanded and they were established.
He set them in place forever and ever; he gave them a boundary, and they do not cross it.
Praise the Lord from the earth, you dragons and all the depths.
Fire and hail, snow and frost, wind and storm, you who carry out his word;
mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars;
wild beasts and all livestock, creeping creatures and all winged birds;
kings of the earth and their armies, rulers and all judges of the earth;
young men and maidens, old men and children;
praise the name of the Lord. His name alone is exalted; praise belongs to him in heaven and on earth.
The Lord raises the horn of his people, praise for all his holy ones, for the children of Israel, the people who are close to the Lord.
Hallelujah.
Praise the Lord with a new song of praise; praise him in the assemblies of the holy ones.
Israel rejoiced in his Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King.
Let them bless his name with praise and psalms, and sing him a psalm of praise.
The Lord delights in his people and exalts the meek with salvation.
Let the holy ones boast in glory and rejoice in their places of rest.
And let them exalt God with their mouths; double-edged swords are in their hands,
to exact retribution from the nations, to rebuke all peoples,
to bind their kings with chains and their mighty men with iron handcuffs,
to carry out the written judgment upon them. This is glory for all his holy ones.
Hallelujah.
Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in the firmament of his power.
Praise him for his might; praise him for his abundant greatness.
Praise him with the sound of praise; praise him with psalms and praise.
Praise him with rejoicing; extol him with gladness.
Praise him with sweet words; praise him with an audible voice; praise him with the sound of thanksgiving.
All spirits, praise the Lord. This psalm was written by David himself, outside the numbering, at the time when he went out as a champion against Goliath before Saul.
I was small among my brothers and the youngest in my father's house; I tended my father's flocks.
My hands made a psaltery, and my fingers fashioned an instrument of praise.
And now, who will tell this to my Lord? The Lord of all himself will hear everything.
He sent his angel and took me from my father’s flock of sheep and anointed me with his anointing oil.
My brothers were handsome and tall, but the Lord was not pleased with them.
I went out to meet the Philistine and cursed his idols.
I drew his sword from him and cut off his head, and removed the disgrace from the children of Israel.
